steps.label: Location and size
steps.detail: Localise the cystic mass and compare with prior size.
findings: [Right] upper-pole cystic mass __ mm, [exophytic / endophytic].
Unchanged in size since [date].
steps.look: Axial and coronal images of both kidneys; the prior study.
steps.tip: Bosniak applies to cystic masses; confirm that the lesion is not a necrotic solid mass or an infection.

steps.label: Contents and enhancement
steps.detail: Assess fluid, haemorrhagic or proteinaceous contents and true enhancement.
findings: Homogeneous fluid attenuation (−9 to 20 HU), no enhancement.
Well-defined homogeneous mass ≥70 HU on unenhanced CT with a smooth thin wall (Bosniak II pattern when the full v2019 criteria are met).
Enhancement of [wall / septa] (increase __ HU).
Heterogeneously hyperintense cystic mass on unenhanced fat-suppressed T1 MRI (Bosniak IIF pattern if no III/IV feature is present).
steps.look: Compare matched precontrast and postcontrast acquisitions: enhancement may be unequivocally visible or quantitatively confirmed (CT increase ≥20 HU; MRI signal increase ≥15% when reliably measurable with the same technique). Check subtraction for motion and misregistration.
steps.tip: Pseudoenhancement, partial volume and subtraction misregistration can mimic enhancement. A feature too small to measure and not clearly visibly enhancing is considered nonenhancing only on adequate source imaging; a non-diagnostic acquisition remains limited.

steps.label: Wall and septa
steps.detail: Describe the number, thickness and smoothness of the wall and septa.
findings: Thin (≤2 mm), smooth wall; no septa (Bosniak I).
1–3 thin enhancing septa (Bosniak II).
Minimally thickened (3 mm) smooth enhancing wall or septum, or ≥4 thin (≤2 mm) smooth enhancing septa (Bosniak IIF).
Thick (≥4 mm) enhancing wall/septa, or irregular enhancing obtuse protrusions ≤3 mm (Bosniak III if no enhancing nodule).
steps.look: Measure the wall and septa perpendicular to their surface on the best-resolved image.

steps.label: Nodules
steps.detail: Characterise enhancing protrusions and their margin with the wall or septum.
findings: Enhancing nodule __ mm with an [acute / obtuse] margin (Bosniak IV).
steps.look: Look for a convex protrusion: 4 mm or larger with an obtuse margin, or any size with an acute margin.

steps.label: Bosniak category
steps.detail: Give the Bosniak 2019 category and the feature that determines it.
findings: Bosniak v2019 category [ ], determined by [feature].

steps.look: The highest-category feature present decides the category.

steps.detail: Describe side, pole, exophytic or endophytic growth and whether the mass is ball- or bean-shaped.
findings: [Right] interpolar ball-shaped solid mass __ × __ mm, [exophytic / endophytic].

steps.look: Axial and coronal images; ball-shaped masses expand the kidney, bean-shaped masses infiltrate and preserve its shape.
steps.tip: Ball-shaped masses are usually renal cell carcinoma or oncocytoma; bean-shaped infiltration suggests urothelial carcinoma, lymphoma, infection or infarction.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Assess macroscopic fat, haemorrhage, calcification and necrosis.
findings: Macroscopic fat within a renal-origin mass, favouring classic angiomyolipoma in the appropriate imaging context; assess calcification, suspicious soft tissue and engulfed adjacent fat.
Central necrosis and calcification.
No macroscopic fat; homogeneous hyperattenuating mass (possible fat-poor angiomyolipoma).
steps.look: Unenhanced CT (fat below −10 HU) or MRI with and without fat suppression.
steps.tip: Macroscopic fat strongly supports classic angiomyolipoma but rare RCC exceptions exist. Opposed-phase signal loss alone does not establish macroscopic fat or a benign diagnosis.

steps.label: Enhancement and signal

findings: Avid heterogeneous enhancement (clear-cell pattern).
Low, homogeneous enhancement with low T2 signal (papillary pattern).
Central scar with segmental enhancement inversion (oncocytoma features, not diagnostic).
steps.look: Corticomedullary and nephrographic phases; T2 signal on MRI.

steps.label: Background liver
steps.detail: Assess liver morphology, steatosis, cirrhosis and the clinical risk context.

normal.BACKGROUND LIVER: Normal liver morphology; no steatosis or cirrhosis.

findings: Cirrhotic morphology with signs of portal hypertension; verify LI-RADS eligibility and exclusions before applying it to observations.
Diffuse hepatic steatosis.
Known primary malignancy: [ ].
steps.look: Liver contour, caudate size, steatosis and signs of portal hypertension.
steps.tip: In a patient without cirrhosis or known cancer most small lesions are benign.

steps.label: Lesion map
steps.detail: Number each lesion and localise it by Couinaud segment.
findings: Lesion 1: segment [ ], __ mm (series __ image __).
Multiple lesions in both lobes, the largest __ mm in segment [ ].
Too small to characterise (under 1 cm) hypodensity in segment [ ].
steps.look: Use the hepatic veins (vertical) and portal vein bifurcation (horizontal) to name segments.
steps.tip: Clinical risk, prior malignancy, lesion features and acquired technique govern interpretation; small size alone cannot establish benignity.

steps.label: Enhancement
steps.detail: Describe arterial and later-phase behaviour.
findings: Peripheral nodular discontinuous enhancement with centripetal fill-in following the blood pool: haemangioma.
Homogeneous arterial enhancement, isoattenuating on later phases, with a central scar: focal nodular hyperplasia.
Arterial enhancement with washout: hepatocellular carcinoma should be considered.
Rim enhancement: metastasis or abscess.
steps.look: Compare the lesion with liver and blood pool on each phase.
steps.tip: A haemangioma follows the blood pool on every phase.

steps.label: Tissue characteristics
steps.detail: Assess fluid, fat, haemorrhage, T2 and diffusion signal and the hepatobiliary phase.
findings: Very high T2 signal (light-bulb), compatible with haemangioma or cyst.
Intralesional fat on opposed-phase images: adenoma or hepatocellular lesion.
Iso- or hyperintense on the hepatobiliary phase: focal nodular hyperplasia.
Restricted diffusion with hypointensity on the hepatobiliary phase.
steps.look: MRI T2, in- and opposed-phase, DWI and hepatobiliary phase when a liver-specific agent was used.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Review bile ducts, vessels, capsular retraction, nodes and extrahepatic disease.

normal.ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: Bile ducts and vessels normal; no extrahepatic disease.

findings: Capsular retraction and peripheral duct dilatation (cholangiocarcinoma pattern).
Portal vein tumour thrombus.
Growth from __ to __ mm since [date].
steps.look: Portal and hepatic veins, bile ducts, the liver capsule and nodes.

steps.label: Eligibility and technique
steps.detail: Confirm the at-risk population, untreated observation and adequate multiphasic technique.
findings: Patient at risk for HCC (cirrhosis); multiphasic MRI with [extracellular / hepatobiliary] agent; adequate arterial phase.
Treated observation: the LI-RADS treatment-response algorithm applies.
steps.look: Cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B or prior HCC; late arterial, portal venous and delayed or transitional phases.
steps.tip: Diagnostic LI-RADS applies only to the at-risk population and untreated observations.

steps.label: Observation map
steps.detail: Identify each observation by segment with its size and prior measurements.
findings: Observation 1: segment [ ], __ mm (previously __ mm on [date]).
steps.look: Measure on the phase where the margin is sharpest, avoiding the arterial phase if possible.

steps.label: Major features
steps.detail: Describe non-rim arterial phase hyperenhancement, washout, enhancing capsule and threshold growth.
findings: Non-rim APHE, washout and an enhancing capsule.
Non-rim APHE without washout or capsule.
Threshold growth: size increase of 50% or more in 6 months or less.
steps.look: Use the acquired late arterial phase for non-rim APHE. Washout: portal venous or delayed phase with extracellular agents or gadobenate; portal venous only with gadoxetate. Transitional or hepatobiliary hypointensity is not washout. Enhancing capsule: assess separately on portal venous, delayed or transitional phases as applicable.

steps.label: LR-M and ancillary features
steps.detail: Assess targetoid features suggesting non-HCC malignancy and ancillary features.
findings: Targetoid appearance (rim APHE, peripheral washout): LR-M.
Ancillary features favouring HCC: [nodule-in-nodule / mosaic architecture / fat / blood products].
Ancillary features favouring benignity: [ ].
steps.look: Rim APHE, peripheral washout, delayed central enhancement, targetoid diffusion; ancillary features such as fat, blood, restricted diffusion.
steps.tip: Ancillary features can adjust the category by one step but cannot upgrade to LR-5.

steps.label: Tumour in vein and category
steps.detail: Assess tumour in vein separately, then give the category and its defining features.
findings: Observation __ mm: non-rim APHE [ ]; nonperipheral washout on eligible phase [ ]; enhancing capsule [ ]; growth [ ]. Category [ ] after applying the v2018 size/feature table and checking LR-M/TIV.
LR-TIV: enhancing tumour in the [right portal vein].
LR-3: intermediate probability of malignancy.
steps.look: Portal and hepatic veins for enhancing soft tissue in the lumen.

classification.name: Revised Atlanta morphology
classification.applicability: Acute pancreatitis and its local complications; clinical severity requires organ-failure information.
classification.summary: Describe interstitial oedematous or necrotising pancreatitis; distinguish acute fluid/necrotic collections from mature pseudocyst or walled-off necrosis.

steps.label: Pancreatic enhancement and necrosis
steps.detail: Distinguish interstitial oedematous pancreatitis from non-enhancing necrosis, with time since onset.

normal.PANCREATIC MORPHOLOGY: Pancreas normal in size and enhancement.

findings: Interstitial oedematous pancreatitis: diffuse enlargement with homogeneous enhancement and peripancreatic stranding.
Necrotising pancreatitis: non-enhancing [body/tail] involving about [<30% / 30–50% / >50%] of the gland.
Extrapancreatic necrosis only, with preserved pancreatic enhancement.
steps.look: Portal venous phase: pancreatic parenchymal enhancement; CT within the first days underestimates necrosis.
steps.tip: Necrosis may not be visible in the first 72 hours; early CT can underestimate it.

steps.label: Collections
steps.detail: Name and describe each collection by location, content, wall and time from onset.
findings: Acute peripancreatic fluid collection in the [lesser sac], __ mm, fluid only, no wall.
Acute necrotic collection __ mm with non-liquid debris.
Walled-off necrosis __ mm with a mature enhancing wall.
Gas within the collection raises concern for infection; correlate with instrumentation and possible enteric fistula.
steps.look: Assess each actual collection: fluid/debris, location, complete or incomplete encapsulation and symptom-onset interval. Do not classify maturity from calendar age alone.
steps.tip: A collection does not automatically become walled-off necrosis on day 28; describe the observed wall and necrotic content. Uncertain content or onset remains explicit.

steps.label: Vascular complications
steps.detail: Search for venous thrombosis, pseudoaneurysm and bleeding.

normal.VASCULAR COMPLICATIONS: Splenic, portal and superior mesenteric veins patent; no pseudoaneurysm.

findings: Splenic vein thrombosis.
Pseudoaneurysm of the [splenic / gastroduodenal] artery, __ mm.
Haemorrhage into a collection.
steps.look: Splenic, portal and superior mesenteric veins; arterial phase for pseudoaneurysm of the splenic or gastroduodenal artery.

steps.label: Duct and cause
steps.detail: Review the main duct, disconnected duct, gallstones and common bile duct obstruction.

normal.DUCTAL AND BILIARY FINDINGS: Main pancreatic duct normal; no gallstones or bile duct dilatation.

findings: Gallstones and bile duct dilatation raise concern for a biliary cause or retained obstruction; assess the actual duct and clinical context.
Necrosis across the pancreatic neck with viable upstream gland, raising concern for disconnected duct.
steps.look: Pancreatic duct continuity through necrosis; gallbladder and common bile duct.

steps.label: Extrapancreatic effects
steps.detail: Assess bowel, ascites, pleural effusions and distant complications.

normal.EXTRAPANCREATIC EFFECTS: No bowel involvement, ascites or pleural effusion.

findings: Ascites and bilateral pleural effusions.
Duodenal compression by the collection.
Colonic wall thickening adjacent to necrosis.
steps.look: Duodenum and colon, peritoneal fluid, pleural bases.

steps.label: Primary tumour and ducts
steps.detail: Localise and measure the tumour and describe duct obstruction and upstream atrophy.
findings: Hypoattenuating mass in the pancreatic [head], __ mm.
Double duct sign: dilated common bile duct and main pancreatic duct.
Upstream parenchymal atrophy.
steps.look: Pancreatic phase for the hypoattenuating tumour; curved reformats of the ducts.
steps.tip: An abrupt duct cut-off with upstream atrophy can indicate a small isoattenuating tumour.

steps.label: Arterial contact
steps.detail: Describe contact with the coeliac axis, common hepatic artery and SMA, including degrees and variant anatomy.

normal.ARTERIAL CONTACT: No contact with the coeliac axis, common hepatic artery or SMA; conventional arterial anatomy.

findings: Tumour contact with the SMA of __° over __ mm.
Encasement of the common hepatic artery (more than 180°).
Replaced right hepatic artery from the SMA.
steps.look: Review adequate pancreatic-protocol contrast phases and planes perpendicular to each vessel; record the actual contact angle, length, contour and named arterial variants. Do not assign resectability from the 180° descriptor alone.
steps.tip: Record variant artery origins, courses and tumour contact explicitly. Name the current resectability framework/version and treatment time point; imaging descriptors require multidisciplinary interpretation.

steps.label: Venous contact
steps.detail: Assess SMV and portal vein contact, contour deformity and occlusion.

normal.VENOUS CONTACT: No contact with the SMV or portal vein.

findings: Contact with the SMV of __° over __ mm without contour deformity.
Tear-drop deformity of the SMV.
Occlusion of the SMV with collateral veins.
steps.look: Review the portal venous phase and orthogonal vessel planes; record contact angle/length, contour, filling defect or occlusion, collateral routes and patent proximal/distal segments. Describe anatomy relevant to possible reconstruction; feasibility requires multidisciplinary surgical assessment.
steps.tip: After neoadjuvant treatment, persistent perivascular soft tissue or venous narrowing is not by itself proof of viable tumour or unresectability. Compare the actual prior examination and state uncertainty.

steps.label: Local extension
steps.detail: Inspect the duodenum, stomach, colon, mesocolon and retroperitoneum.
findings: Extension into the root of the mesentery.
Invasion of the duodenal wall.
Infiltrating soft tissue along the [named perivascular/neural pathway], concerning for perineural spread; CT does not establish microscopic invasion.
steps.look: Fat planes around the tumour and along the mesentery root.

steps.label: Metastatic disease
steps.detail: Assess the liver, peritoneum, nodes and other distant sites.

normal.METASTATIC DISEASE: No liver or peritoneal metastases; no suspicious nodes.

findings: Hypoattenuating liver lesions suspicious for metastases.
Ascites with peritoneal nodularity.
Suspicious para-aortic node (distant).
steps.look: Liver on portal venous phase; peritoneum and ascites; regional and distant nodes.
steps.tip: Resectability requires vessel, local-extension and metastatic review under a stated current framework and multidisciplinary judgement. Tumour size or contact angle alone is insufficient, especially after treatment.

measurements.pitfall: Apparent nodule size can include adjacent wall or nonenhancing debris.

classification.name: IPMN risk assessment — framework-qualified descriptors
classification.applicability: Presumed IPMN; not a universal algorithm for all pancreatic cysts or proof of histological malignancy.
classification.summary: For presumed IPMN, assess actual nodule/solid-component enhancement and exact duct calibre under the named framework. Imaging risk findings require clinical/cytological context and specialist assessment; this overview is not the complete guideline.

pitfalls: A pseudocyst diagnosis needs a compatible clinical context; cyst classification is separate from solid pancreatic cancer staging.
Duct communication alone does not establish IPMN; inflammatory collections may also communicate.
Presumed cyst type alone does not mandate resection; distinguish framework-specific assessment and complete clinical suitability.
Subtraction artifact, debris and wall partial volume can mimic a nodule; adequate source enhancement evidence is required.

headings: Where to look for Peritoneal Carcinomatosis

protocol: Check T2, high-b DWI/ADC and DCE quality separately and record prior biopsy/treatment.
Use the comprehensive prostate template; match lesion numbers and sector locations across every sequence.

Retain native sequence/plane, source spatial sampling, examination extent and quality. Distinguish acquired diffusion, producer-derived ADC/calculated DWI, source DCE and actual contrast timing; shared frame identifiers do not establish every registration or fine-tissue resolution.

checklist.label: Clinical context
checklist.detail: Review the complete acquired gland, base/mid/apex, separate PZ/TZ/CZ and anterior fibromuscular stroma, periurethral tissue, haemorrhage and BPH components. Record actual dimensions, volume method, dated PSA and source quality; unavailable tissue is unassessed.

checklist.label: Zonal anatomy
checklist.detail: Map every actually reported finding across all involved native sectors and levels, with complete components, margins, maximum dimension, source series/plane and neighbours. PI-RADS v2.1 has41 regions:38 prostate, two seminal-vesicle and one external-sphincter regions; the diagram is an idealized map, not patient geometry.

checklist.label: Scoring
checklist.detail: Assess actual T2, acquired or calculated high-b DWI, ADC and any DCE separately, with quality, ROI, calibration, timing and motion limits. Apply applicable v2.1 sequence/zone rules only after adequate observations; a source Likert score, ROI, size alone or uncalibrated ADC value does not supply a current assessment.

checklist.label: Local extension
checklist.detail: Trace each source-resolved lesion/glandular-surface interface, TZ/PZ pseudocapsule, anterior/apical gaps, bilateral nerves/vessels, seminal vesicles and ducts, bladder neck, urethra, external sphincter, fascia and rectal interfaces. Record actual contact and direct extension separately; the prostate has no complete true capsule.

checklist.label: Beyond gland
checklist.detail: Review every acquired pelvic node and basin, cortex/hilum and vascular relationship, imaged bones, bladder, rectum and other reported pelvic findings. Preserve actual field coverage, clinical/tissue and treatment evidence; no unacquired nodal/bone survey or whole-gland shape supplies a negative result or current stage.

measurements.name: Gland volume and PSA density
measurements.method: Use ellipsoid AP×transverse×longitudinal×0.52 in cm or segmentation; PSA density=PSA/volume.
measurements.pitfall: Record the PSA date and volume method; density is not a PI-RADS scoring input.

measurements.name: Lesion dimension
measurements.method: Measure largest dimension on ADC for PZ or T2 for TZ where adequately defined; record plane/sequence.
measurements.pitfall: DWI score 5 needs the specified ≥1.5 cm size or definite invasive behaviour criterion.

measurements.name: Capsular contact
measurements.method: Record contact length and direct extension findings separately.
measurements.pitfall: Contact length alone does not prove extraprostatic extension.

measurements.name: Each actual source component and interface
measurements.method: Record the supplied native plane/sequence, acquisition axes, calibration, each component/total extent and actual adjacent structures. Separate source measurements and dated clinical/pathological information.
measurements.pitfall: Voxel pitch, a source ROI, sector map or complete organ outline does not establish microscopic interfaces, complete tumour extent or current stage.

classification.name: PI-RADS
classification.applicability: Detection and localisation of clinically significant prostate cancer in the untreated prostate using an adequate examination.
classification.summary: Use the zone-specific dominant sequence and published adjustment rules. The category expresses suspicion, separately from PSA density, stage and management.

pitfalls: Prostatitis, BPH nodules and haemorrhage can imitate cancer.
PI-RADS v2.1 is not the post-treatment recurrence scoring system.
Prostate outer fibromuscular boundary and TZ/PZ pseudocapsule are distinct and neither is a complete true histological capsule.
The official41-sector map is an idealized localization aid. Each source patient and every actual lesion, route, boundary and variant requires its own geometry.

Published suspicious target ROIs and source Likert-like scores are not proven tumour extent or automatic current PI-RADS v2.1 assessments. Unavailable ADC calibration, native high-b data or DCE remain explicit.
impression_prompts: State index lesion number, sector and PI-RADS category.
Summarise local extension and pelvic findings separately from suspicion score.
Record gland volume, PSA density when available and material image-quality limits.

sections.heading: SCORING CHECK
sections.body:
PZ: DWI determines the category; DWI 3 becomes PI-RADS 4 only with positive DCE. Positive DCE requires focal early enhancement corresponding to the suspicious finding.
TZ: T2 determines the category, except T2 2 with DWI ≥4 becomes PI-RADS 3, and T2 3 with DWI 5 becomes PI-RADS 4. DCE does not upgrade TZ lesions.
A score-4-pattern lesion is score 5 on the relevant sequence at ≥1.5 cm or with definite extraprostatic extension/invasion.
No DCE means no DCE-based upgrade. If DWI is inadequate, consult the PI-RADS alternative-assessment table and state the limitation.

notes: PI-RADS categories express imaging suspicion: 1 very low; 2 low; 3 equivocal; 4 high; 5 very high likelihood of clinically significant cancer. They do not independently prescribe biopsy or treatment.
Choose the index lesion by highest PI-RADS category; resolve ties by extraprostatic extension, then size. Map up to four principal suspicious lesions and identify all sectors involved.
Measure AP and longitudinal gland dimensions on mid-sagittal T2, transverse on axial T2. Avoid mixing millimetres and centimetres in the ellipsoid formula.
PI-RADS diagnostic scoring is not a post-treatment recurrence system. A negative MRI does not exclude clinically significant cancer; interpret with clinical risk.
If both DWI and DCE are unavailable or inadequate, do not imply a complete PI-RADS assessment; the formal guidance limits assessment to staging for extraprostatic extension.
Use actual study images in the image slots and retain matching series/image references in the report.

protocol: Record screening/diagnostic purpose, side, actual digital mammography, tomosynthesis, synthetic or contrast-enhanced acquisitions and views. Identify compression, positioning, obtained tissue, motion and obscured extent; density and enhancement are different observations.

Record every relevant source population, age/development, hormonal/lactation, intervention and dated comparison context. Source views, planes and tissue confirmation are separate evidence; unrelated patients and modalities are not implicitly registered.

checklist.label: Composition
checklist.detail: Map actual bilateral composition and obtained skin-to-chest-wall tissue, including nipple, retroareolar ducts and axillary tail. Preserve view and depth; a compressed projection is not native3D geometry.

checklist.label: Mass
checklist.detail: Locate each actual mass and all internal, marginal and adjacent components using acquired projections or tomosynthesis; document site, dimensions and evidence for cross-view correspondence.

checklist.label: Other findings
checklist.detail: Trace each acquired asymmetry and distortion, its centre, radiating tissue and adjacent interfaces; compare dated studies and actual additional views without treating unacquired workup as negative.

checklist.label: Change
checklist.detail: Map every actual calcification group, individual resolved morphology/distribution, span, skin/duct/lesion relation and associated nipple, skin or node finding. A selected projection does not resolve every microscopic boundary.

checklist.label: Assessment
checklist.detail: Reconcile each imaging and clinical site, prior intervention and obtained other modality. Record unresolved discordance and assessment rationale under the applicable current framework; source morphology is not current histology.

measurements.name: Finding size
measurements.method: Measure the maximum dimension on the view best showing its boundary.
measurements.pitfall: Magnification and projection changes affect apparent size.

measurements.name: Distribution/span
measurements.method: Measure calcification or related abnormality extent and record depth.
measurements.pitfall: A single mass measurement may underestimate total abnormal tissue.

measurements.name: Source finding and every relevant interface

measurements.name: Mapping

pitfalls: Incomplete coverage, arrhythmia and contour convention can change apparent volume/function; no normal quantitative result is inferred from a still or unavailable sequence.

Ischaemic-type LGE commonly involves subendocardium in a coronary distribution; other patterns, global subendocardial involvement, mixed disease and acquisition artefact require a differential, not an exclusive cause.
Absent LGE does not exclude every cardiomyopathy or diffuse tissue abnormality. Poor nulling/ghosting/partial volume can mimic or obscure enhancement.
Map colours or another scanner/site threshold are not independently calibrated normality; actual raw source quality and reference method matter.
Static jet, effusion or filling-defect appearance does not quantify regurgitation, tamponade or prove thrombus; appropriate functional/tissue/clinical evidence is separate.

Summarise tissue/LGE pattern and the supported differential.
Identify clinically consequential thrombus, valve or pericardial findings.
escalation: Communicate an unexpected intracardiac thrombus or another acutely consequential finding directly.

steps.detail: Quantify both ventricles from the short-axis cine stack.
findings: Dilated left ventricle (LVEDVi __ mL/m²) with reduced ejection fraction (__%).
Right ventricular dilatation with reduced RVEF __%.
steps.look: Short-axis cine from base to apex; contour end diastole and end systole; compare with sex- and age-specific references.
steps.tip: Quantify actual temporal/source contours with complete coverage; document ED/ES and basal/apical/papillary/trabecular conventions plus reference/indexing context. Do not infer EF or normality from a still/model.

steps.label: Wall thickness and regional motion
steps.detail: Assess wall thickness, mass and regional wall motion by segment.
findings: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy with maximal wall thickness __ mm at [basal anteroseptum].
Akinesia of the [anterior] wall in the [LAD] territory.
Apical ballooning with basal hyperkinesia (takotsubo pattern).
steps.look: Inspect obtained short/long-axis cines with actual named segment/region and apical coverage; state the model/convention and any region where motion/thickening cannot be assessed.
steps.tip: Locate actual maximal thickness and distinguish endocardial/trabecular/papillary boundaries from compact myocardium; phase and source sampling limit thin regions.

steps.label: Oedema and mapping
steps.detail: Review T2-weighted oedema, native T1 and T2 mapping and ECV if acquired.
findings: Regional oedema in the [ ] segments with raised T2 (__ ms).
Diffusely raised native T1 (__ ms) and ECV (__%).
steps.look: T2-weighted and mapping sequences with the local reference range and field strength.
steps.tip: Mapping and ECV require actual sequence/field strength, raw-source/ROI quality and comparable references. ECV identifies its haematocrit/date or explicitly named alternative method; colour pictures are not calibrated measurements.

steps.label: Late gadolinium enhancement
steps.detail: Map LGE by segment, layer, transmurality and coronary territory.
findings: Subendocardial / transmural LGE in the [LAD] territory, __% transmural (ischaemic pattern).
Midwall LGE in the septum (non-ischaemic pattern).
Subepicardial LGE in the inferolateral wall (myocarditis pattern).
Patchy LGE at the RV insertion points in hypertrophied segments (HCM pattern).
steps.look: Short- and long-axis LGE in matching planes; check the myocardium is correctly nulled.
steps.tip: Coronary-pattern subendocardial LGE supports an ischaemic differential, but global subendocardial, midwall/epicardial, mixed or artefactual patterns do not uniquely establish cause. Absent LGE does not exclude all cardiomyopathy; record nulling, quality and actual coverage.

Mitral regurgitation jet on cine.
steps.look: Long-axis cines and early post-contrast images for thrombus.

measurements.name: Stenosis
measurements.method: Compare the minimum orthogonal lumen with an appropriate reference segment.
measurements.pitfall: Calcific blooming and motion can overestimate narrowing.

measurements.name: Plaque burden
measurements.method: Record CAC and/or plaque-containing segment count; use the most severe reliable burden method.
measurements.pitfall: Zero CAC does not exclude non-calcified plaque.

measurements.name: CT-FFR
measurements.method: Record lesion-specific value 1–2 cm beyond the lesion and distinguish the distal nadir.
measurements.pitfall: The lowest distal value alone should not drive lesion attribution.

classification.name: CAD-RADS
classification.applicability: Coronary CTA interpreted with the full diagnostic quality and clinical context.
classification.summary: Report stenosis category with plaque burden and applicable N, HRP, I, S, G or E modifiers. CAD-RADS 0 has no plaque burden category.

pitfalls: HRP requires at least two specified high-risk plaque features in a plaque.
When a relevant segment is non-diagnostic, apply the N category/modifier rules rather than treating it as normal.
impression_prompts: State the most important stenosis and its vessel/segment.
Summarise plaque burden and the complete applicable CAD-RADS 2.0 notation.
Describe anomaly, graft/stent, physiology and significant extracardiac findings.
escalation: Communicate a suspected acute coronary complication or critical unexpected coronary anatomy in the relevant clinical context.

criteria_table.scope: Apply after reviewing all evaluable segments. Plaque burden, HRP, physiology and other modifiers are separate; use the complete report template for those rules.

rows.criteria: No coronary plaque or stenosis.
rows.report_note: Do not append a P category.

rows.report_note: Describe the plaque.

rows.criteria: 25–49% stenosis.
rows.report_note: Record the dominant lesion.

rows.criteria: 50–69% stenosis.
rows.report_note: Correlate with symptoms and any physiology.

rows.criteria: 70–99% stenosis in one or two vessels.
rows.report_note: Specify vessel and segment.

rows.criteria: Left main ≥50%, or severe three-vessel disease.
rows.report_note: State the qualifying anatomy.

rows.criteria: At least one total occlusion.
rows.report_note: Describe occlusion and distal vessel.

rows.criteria: Relevant segment non-evaluable; no ≥50% stenosis shown elsewhere.
rows.report_note: If ≥50% is demonstrated elsewhere, retain that category and add N.

steps.label: Calcium score
steps.detail: If a non-contrast scan was acquired, record the total and per-vessel Agatston scores.

normal.CALCIUM SCORE: CAC: total 0 Agatston units (LM 0 | LAD 0 | LCx 0 | RCA 0). A zero CAC score does not exclude non-calcified plaque.

findings: CAC: total ___ Agatston units (LM ___ | LAD ___ | LCx ___ | RCA ___).
CAC: not performed.
steps.look: Non-contrast ECG-triggered images; confirm that each calcified focus is assigned to the correct vessel before accepting the total.
steps.tip: Agatston scoring is defined on the non-contrast acquisition; do not derive it from contrast-enhanced images.
steps.anatomy_note: Gross artery surfaces provide orientation only. They do not depict calcific foci or permit Agatston scoring; use the acquired non-contrast CT.

steps.label: Dominance and anatomy
steps.detail: Establish dominance, origins, proximal course and coronary anomalies.

normal.CORONARY ORIGINS / COURSE: Normal origins of the left main and right coronary arteries from the left and right coronary sinuses, with a normal proximal course. No myocardial bridge or fistula.

findings: Anomalous origin of the [RCA / LCA] from the [opposite / non-coronary] sinus with an [interarterial / retroaortic / prepulmonic / septal] course.
High-risk anomaly features: [slit-like ostium / acute take-off / intramural segment / proximal narrowing].
Myocardial bridge of the [mid LAD], __ mm long and __ mm deep.
Coronary artery fistula from the [ ] to the [ ].
steps.look: Axial source images and volume rendering at the sinuses of Valsalva; follow each ostium and its proximal course relative to the aorta and pulmonary trunk; find which artery supplies the PDA.
steps.tip: Name an interarterial course between the aorta and pulmonary trunk explicitly, with any intramural segment or slit-like ostium.
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross left/right coronary trunks, LAD, circumflex and an RCA-derived posterior branch are available. Individual ostia, sinus anatomy, branch origins and anomalous courses are not independently resolved. Determine patient dominance from the images; do not assume the example circulation.

steps.label: Stenosis by segment
steps.detail: Record vessel and segment, plaque composition and the highest confident stenosis category.

normal.CORONARY FINDINGS: LM, LAD and diagonal branches, LCx and obtuse marginal branches, and RCA/PDA/PLV: no plaque or stenosis.

findings: [Vessel/segment]: [calcified / non-calcified / partially calcified] plaque with [minimal 1–24% / mild 25–49% / moderate 50–69% / severe 70–99%] stenosis; series __ image __.
[Vessel/segment]: total occlusion, __ mm long, [with / without] distal reconstitution.
[Segment] non-diagnostic because of [motion / blooming calcification / poor opacification]; significant stenosis cannot be excluded.
steps.look: Curved MPR along each vessel, then orthogonal cross-sections at the tightest point and at a normal reference segment; check the axial source images for artefact.
steps.tip: Blooming from dense calcification overestimates stenosis; grade on orthogonal cross-sections with a wide window.
steps.anatomy_note: Gross artery surfaces do not establish the lumen, reference diameter, individual branch segments, plaque or stenosis. Use acquired orthogonal CT lumen sections and document non-evaluable segments.

steps.label: Plaque and burden
steps.detail: Describe plaque type and high-risk features, then state burden with the method used; no plaque is not P1.

normal.PLAQUE BURDEN: No plaque; no plaque-burden category is assigned.

findings: High-risk plaque in the [segment]: [positive remodelling / low attenuation / spotty calcification / napkin-ring sign]; at least two features are present, so the HRP modifier applies.
Predominantly [calcified / non-calcified / partially calcified] plaque in __ segments.
Segment involvement score __ ([method]); overall plaque burden P__.
steps.look: Cross-sections through each plaque for attenuation, remodelling and spotty calcification; count plaque-containing segments for SIS, or use the CAC score.
steps.tip: HRP needs at least two high-risk features within the same plaque.
steps.anatomy_note: No plaque geometry, calcific distribution or high-risk plaque morphology is represented in this atlas. Normal surface meshes cannot prove absence of plaque or its burden.

steps.label: Stents, grafts and physiology
steps.detail: Assess stent and graft patency, and record CT-FFR or perfusion when available.

normal.STENTS / GRAFTS: No coronary stents or bypass grafts.

findings: Stent in the [vessel/segment]: [patent / in-stent restenosis __% / occluded / non-diagnostic].
[LIMA / RIMA / SVG] to [target]: [patent / stenosis at __ / occluded]; distal anastomosis [ ].
CT-FFR __ measured 1–2 cm distal to the [segment] lesion; lowest distal value __ in [vessel].
steps.look: Sharp-kernel reconstructions with a wide window for the stent lumen; follow each graft from origin through its body to the distal anastomosis and run-off.
steps.tip: Report the lesion-specific CT-FFR value 1–2 cm beyond the lesion, separately from the lowest distal value.
steps.anatomy_note: Stents, grafts, anastomoses and physiological measurements are not supplied by these meshes. The source aorta and coronary trunks are orientation context only.

steps.label: Cardiac and extracardiac findings
steps.detail: Review chambers, valves, pericardium, aorta and the whole acquired field of view.

normal.EXTRACORONARY CARDIAC FINDINGS: Cardiac chambers normal in size; pericardium normal; no significant valvular calcification; aortic root and ascending aorta normal in calibre.
normal.EXTRACARDIAC FINDINGS: No significant finding in the imaged lungs, mediastinum, upper abdomen or bones.

findings: Aortic valve calcification, [mild / moderate / severe].
Pulmonary nodule __ mm in the [lobe]; follow-up according to the applicable guideline.
Pericardial effusion, [small / moderate].
steps.look: A full field-of-view reconstruction, not only the cardiac field, in lung and soft-tissue windows.
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross ventricular/atrial wall and ascending-aorta context is highlighted. Valves, pericardial layers, coronary sinuses, lungs and other acquired extracardiac anatomy are not independently represented.

steps.label: CAD-RADS 2.0
steps.detail: Assign the final category, plaque burden and modifiers from the findings already recorded.
findings: Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS __/P__ [/HRP] [/S] [/G] [/I+ / I− / I±] [/E].
Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS N — non-diagnostic; obstructive disease cannot be excluded.
steps.look: Use the highest-grade stenosis from the segment review, the burden step and each applicable modifier (N, HRP, I, S, G, E).
steps.tip: The category follows the highest-grade stenosis; when reliable burden methods disagree, use the most severe.
steps.anatomy_note: The atlas supplies anatomical orientation only. CAD-RADS, plaque burden, diagnostic quality and physiology must follow acquired evidence; a mesh selection cannot establish the classification.

steps.look: Unenhanced and arterial phase images from the root to the iliacs; sagittal oblique reformats.
steps.tip: Classic Stanford classification is based on ascending-aortic involvement, irrespective of tear origin. Describe arch-only/atypical patterns and the named framework explicitly; immediately communicate suspected acute aortic syndrome, rupture or malperfusion.

steps.label: Dissection, intramural haematoma or ulcer
steps.detail: Distinguish dissection with a flap from intramural haematoma and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer.

steps.look: Unenhanced images for crescentic hyperattenuating wall thickening; contrast images for flap, lumina and ulceration.
steps.tip: Beak/cobweb morphology and continuity with undissected aorta can support lumen identification. Confirm actual source course, enhancement phase and thrombus; lumen size alone is not definitive, and IMH, tiny tears or ulcerative features may overlap.

checklist.detail: Describe each vascular/ductal component around the trachea and oesophagus, compression level and length, and associated tracheobronchial branching or cartilage abnormalities; distinguish directly seen from inferred ring components.

checklist.label: Pulmonary arteries
checklist.detail: Trace each actual pulmonary artery origin, proximal and covered distal course; distinguish proximal interruption from whole-lung agenesis, identify sling, systemic collaterals and ductal connection.

checklist.label: Pulmonary veins

measurements.name: Vessel calibre
measurements.method: Measure the minimum orthogonal diameter at named segments, such as a coarctation and the adjacent normal aorta.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique axial measurements overestimate calibre; use a plane perpendicular to the vessel.

measurements.name: Airway narrowing
measurements.method: Measure the minimum tracheal or bronchial lumen at the level of compression and its length.
measurements.pitfall: Expiratory phase and patient position change airway calibre.

pitfalls: A complete ring depends on the actual arch, branch and ductal/ligamentous configuration; a non-opacified or atretic component may be inferred from secondary signs but must not be presented as directly visualised.
Poor opacification or incomplete coverage does not establish absence. Tailor acquisition to the clinical question rather than automatically adding a delayed radiation exposure.
Static CT/MRI airway narrowing does not establish dynamic malacia or its clinical severity; respiratory phase and appropriate dynamic/bronchoscopic assessment matter.
Pulmonary venous number and drainage vary; four separate ostia are not required for normal anatomy. Trace accessory/common/dual channels before labelling return normal.
Persistent left SVC can drain to the coronary sinus/right atrium or to the left atrium; confirm the actual endpoint and relevant coronary-sinus/septal anatomy.
impression_prompts: What is the vascular anomaly and does it form a ring or sling?
Is the trachea or oesophagus compressed, and where?
Are there associated pulmonary venous or systemic venous anomalies or a shunt?
escalation: Communicate critical airway compression or a severe coarctation promptly.

steps.label: Aortic arch
steps.detail: Establish arch side, branching order, aberrant subclavian artery, diverticulum, double arch and coarctation.
findings: Right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery arising from a Kommerell diverticulum (__ mm).
Left arch with aberrant right subclavian artery passing behind the oesophagus.
Double aortic arch with a dominant [right] arch.
Coarctation distal to the left subclavian artery, minimum diameter __ mm, with collaterals.
steps.look: Axial images above the arch for the four-artery sign; volume rendering of the arch and branches.
steps.tip: Describe each patent or inferred atretic component and ductal/ligamentous attachment. The four-artery sign and flat volume rendering do not independently prove all ring components or the actual anomaly geometry.

steps.label: Airway and oesophagus
steps.detail: Look for a vascular ring or sling compressing the trachea or oesophagus.
findings: Tracheal narrowing to __ mm at the level of the [double arch / innominate artery].
Posterior oesophageal impression by the aberrant subclavian artery.
steps.look: Minimum-intensity projections of the trachea; oesophagus behind the arch.
steps.tip: Record respiratory phase and actual level/length of narrowing. Static narrowing alone does not diagnose dynamic tracheobronchomalacia; cartilage and bronchial anomalies require source-resolved assessment.

steps.label: Pulmonary arteries
steps.detail: Assess the pulmonary artery origin and course, agenesis, sling and patent ductus.
findings: Left pulmonary artery arises from the right pulmonary artery and passes between the trachea and oesophagus (pulmonary sling).
Unilateral pulmonary artery [agenesis / hypoplasia].
Patent ductus arteriosus.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images of the main and branch pulmonary arteries.
steps.tip: Distinguish proximal pulmonary artery interruption from absence of lung and bronchus; trace distal arteries and systemic collateral supply. Ductal patency/flow needs adequate acquisition and appropriate functional evidence.

steps.label: Pulmonary veins
steps.detail: Trace every pulmonary vein to its drainage and look for anomalous return.
findings: Partial anomalous return of the right upper-lobe vein to the superior vena cava (often with a sinus venosus defect).
Scimitar vein draining the right lung to the IVC.
Left upper-lobe vein draining via a vertical vein to the brachiocephalic vein.
steps.look: Trace each actual lobar/segmental venous channel, common/accessory trunks, dual drainage and the complete collector route to its atrial or systemic endpoint. Record opacification and coverage limits.
steps.tip: Do not assume four separate pulmonary veins. Morphology and right-heart enlargement do not quantify shunt flow or determine haemodynamic significance. Single-phase contrast density does not independently quantify flow direction or Qp/Qs; report the actual functional source.

steps.label: Systemic veins
steps.detail: Identify a left superior vena cava, azygos continuation of the IVC and the left superior intercostal vein.
findings: Persistent left superior vena cava draining into a dilated coronary sinus.
Azygos continuation of the IVC with an enlarged azygos arch.
Prominent left superior intercostal vein (aortic nipple).
steps.look: Follow each SVC and bridging vein to its actual endpoint, assess the coronary sinus/septum and trace covered IVC/hepatic and azygos/hemiazygos connections.
steps.tip: A left SVC usually drains through the coronary sinus to the right atrium, but left-atrial drainage occurs. Do not infer its endpoint from a single left mediastinal vessel or coronary-sinus enlargement. Trace vertical/levoatriocardinal, pericardiophrenic and postoperative mimics to their actual endpoints; single-phase density is not a calibrated flow measurement.

measurements.name: Aortic annulus
measurements.method: Identify the virtual basal/hinge plane from the actual cusp attachment nadirs in multiplanar imaging; measure the annular contour and orthogonal dimensions in the stated phase. Record variant anatomy and unresolved nadirs.
measurements.pitfall: A fixed one-slice offset or the last visible leaflet is not a reproducible basal-plane definition; slice thickness, phase and cusp/valve morphology matter.

measurements.name: Sinus of Valsalva
measurements.method: Record the maximum sinus-to-sinus root diameter on the appropriate short-axis plane, with named edge convention and cardiac phase. Report multiple dimensions for an asymmetric root; retain any legacy average or alternative axis separately for comparison.
measurements.pitfall: Sinus-to-commissure, mid/maximum sinus-to-sinus and averages are not interchangeable; an average must not silently replace the maximum root diameter.

measurements.name: Thoracic aortic diameter
measurements.method: Use a plane perpendicular to the local aortic axis at every named level. For CT/MRI root and ascending assessment, record inner-edge measurements with ECG synchronisation; report outer-edge dimensions for abnormal thickened wall segments, retaining the actual convention.
measurements.pitfall: Axial slices cut the curved aorta obliquely and give elliptical, overestimated diameters.

measurements.name: Interval change
measurements.method: Compare the same level on the prior study using the same modality and method; give the change in millimetres and the interval.
measurements.pitfall: Small differences can reflect acquisition, phase, edge or plane variability; record comparability and uncertainty before assigning growth or applying clinical thresholds.

pitfalls: Raw axial sections may obliquely sample a curved aorta; retain orthogonal plane/centreline and selected level.
Edge conventions, cardiac phase and root-axis/summary method are not interchangeable; preserve maximal and asymmetric dimensions.
TTE leading-edge and CT/MRI inner/outer-edge methods have different conventions; document the actual method and patient/reference framework rather than treating all values as equivalent.
impression_prompts: What is the maximal diameter, at which level and by which method?
Is the aorta dilated against the sex-specific reference values used locally?
What has changed since the previous study measured the same way, and over what interval?
escalation: Communicate rapid growth, or a diameter at the local surgical threshold, to the referring team.

checklist.detail: Localise every actual lesion/pseudomass to its chamber, wall, valve, septum, vessel or pericardial/extracardiac origin; trace each attachment and adjacent interface with unresolved extent recorded.

checklist.label: Morphology
checklist.detail: Describe each lesion component, orthogonal dimensions, contour, stalk/base and local spread; mobility or prolapse requires actual temporal acquisition, not a static picture.

checklist.label: Tissue Characteristics
checklist.detail: Describe actual CT attenuation/calcification and MRI fat, blood, fluid/fibrous or other signal components with sequence, phase, calibration and reference tissues; appearances alone are not histology.

checklist.label: Enhancement
checklist.detail: Assess only obtained first-pass, early/delayed or late enhancement and persistence of filling defects with actual timing/sequence quality; lack of enhancement or a single phase is not a universal diagnosis.

checklist.label: Effects And Spread
checklist.detail: Assess every relevant valve/inflow/outflow, coronary/venous and wall/pericardial interface, obstruction or invasive feature, and covered extracardiac sites; haemodynamic significance and staging need actual source evidence.

measurements.name: Mass dimensions
measurements.method: Measure in orthogonal planes and distinguish attachment from the mobile component.
measurements.pitfall: Cardiac phase and motion can alter apparent size.

pitfalls: Normal ridges, trabeculations, valve remnants, aneurysms and extracardiac structures can mimic a lesion; trace the actual structure and adjacent anatomy.
Thrombus usually lacks enhancement, but organised chronic thrombus can rarely show peripheral enhancement. Tumour-associated thrombus and mixed components must be assessed separately.
A single early filling defect may reflect mixing; resolution/persistence needs appropriate actual timing and quality. Additional phases are not automatic.
Signal, enhancement, FDG uptake, size or attachment pattern alone does not prove tumour type or malignancy; clinical/operative/pathology context and uncertainty matter.
Static position, effusion or apparent narrowing does not quantify mobility, obstruction, regurgitation, haemodynamic significance or tamponade.
impression_prompts: Cardiac mass location, tissue features and non-neoplastic mimics.
State the dominant abnormality, relevant extent and examination limitations.
escalation: Communicate source-supported critical obstruction, suspected embolic complication, severe clinically concerning pericardial involvement or other urgent finding through the actual clinical pathway; record uncertainty and required clinical assessment.

protocol: Record the actual clinical question, symptom/limb-threat context supplied by the clinical team, side, acquired arterial territory and prior intervention. State CE-MRA or actual noncontrast method, source sequences and per-station coverage/quality.

Record source voxel calibration and acquired versus reconstructed resolution, mask/arterial phases, station overlap and contrast agent/dose/timing if given. Use original source images with multiple reconstructions; unperformed acquisitions and uncovered segments remain unassessed.

checklist.label: Inflow
checklist.detail: Trace the actually covered aortic and iliac inflow, each side and branch configuration; identify unassessed proximal segments.

checklist.label: Segmental Disease
checklist.detail: Map every covered common/deep/superficial femoral and popliteal segment, lesion and variant by side and actual anatomical endpoints.

checklist.label: Lesion Morphology
checklist.detail: Describe each lesion and its native-source minimum lumen, reference, length, morphology and uncertainty; distinguish signal loss from confirmed occlusion.

checklist.label: Runoff And Collaterals
checklist.detail: Trace each actual tibial/peroneal artery to its resolved distal endpoint and each pedal/plantar connection, collateral and reconstitution; do not assume three patent channels.

checklist.label: Technical Limitations
checklist.detail: State per-station acquisition, coverage, source quality, contrast/flow timing, venous overlap and artefact; distinguish a non-diagnostic segment from disease.

measurements.name: Lesion length
measurements.method: Measure each lesion along its actual vessel axis between named source-supported proximal/distal landmarks; record minimum orthogonal lumen, reference site/convention, units and uncertainty if assessed.
measurements.pitfall: Signal loss is not automatically occlusion; an unsupported percentage or projection width is not a calibrated lumen measurement.

pitfalls: An unopacified or uncovered artery is not automatically absent or occluded. Record variant origins and the source evidence for lumen continuity.
Branch names describe actual observed anatomy; hypoplasia, high origin, trifurcation, dominant peroneal supply and postoperative anatomy must be traced rather than substituted with a normal tree.

Stenosis percentage requires a stated measurement/reference convention and adequate native source. MIP overlap, subtraction and flow or metal artefacts can mimic or exaggerate disease; missing lumen evidence remains uncertain.

Tibial channel count does not establish uninterrupted supply to the foot, a complete pedal arch, wound perfusion or tissue viability. Morphological continuity does not by itself establish flow direction, pressure or clinical effect.

Historical scanner/coil, injection, compression-cuff and pixel-count advice is not a universal current protocol or safety clearance. Suspected acute limb ischaemia requires urgent clinical assessment; do not delay care to obtain a routine MRA.
impression_prompts: Summarise dominant source-supported disease by side, named segment, extent and actual distal continuity.
Describe variants, intervention anatomy and confidence; identify unanswered distal-target or clinical questions and non-diagnostic/uncovered segments.
Do not infer haemodynamic severity, wound perfusion, limb viability or treatment outcome from a static angiographic appearance.
escalation: Urgently communicate source findings and limitations when acute limb ischaemia or threatened limb is suspected; clinical viability assessment and management should not be delayed for routine MRA.

measurements.name: Main pulmonary artery
measurements.method: Measure source-resolved PA perpendicular to its local axis at a named level and source phase; use a stated ascending-aortic/reference measurement method and edge convention if ratio is reported.
measurements.pitfall: PA diameter/ratio alone does not diagnose haemodynamic PH or establish a clinical group; motion and contrast/coverage limits remain.

pitfalls: Absent contrast or severe motion is a technical limitation, not proof of occlusion or a negative embolic examination. Record affected segments and unresolved defect/mixing boundaries.

Acute emboli may be eccentric as well as central. No location/angle alone dates a clot or excludes acute-on-chronic disease; distinguish source filling defects from motion, mixing, partial-volume or other mimics.

CTEPD may occur without PH; CT chronic morphology alone does not establish CTEPH or operability. A limited or negative CTPA does not alone exclude distal chronic disease; clinical/perfusion assessment is separate.

CT dimensions, RV/LV, septal shape and reflux suggest morphology, not measured pressure or EF. In the named 2022 ESC/ERS definition PH requires resting mPAP >20 mmHg by haemodynamic source; precapillary pattern also requires PAWP ≤15 mmHg and PVR >2 WU. No such values are inferred from CT.

Emphysema/fibrosis, mosaic attenuation, septal thickening or a filling mass are differential clues, not automatic WHO-group, PVOD, sarcoma, infarct or viability diagnoses. Trace actual connections and retain clinical/tissue/functional uncertainty; no treatment choice is made from the companion model.

notes: Absent contrast or severe motion is a technical limitation, not proof of occlusion or a negative embolic examination. Record affected segments and unresolved defect/mixing boundaries.

Acute emboli may be eccentric as well as central. No location/angle alone dates a clot or excludes acute-on-chronic disease; distinguish source filling defects from motion, mixing, partial-volume or other mimics.

CTEPD may occur without PH; CT chronic morphology alone does not establish CTEPH or operability. A limited or negative CTPA does not alone exclude distal chronic disease; clinical/perfusion assessment is separate.

CT dimensions, RV/LV, septal shape and reflux suggest morphology, not measured pressure or EF. In the named 2022 ESC/ERS definition PH requires resting mPAP >20 mmHg by haemodynamic source; precapillary pattern also requires PAWP ≤15 mmHg and PVR >2 WU. No such values are inferred from CT.

Emphysema/fibrosis, mosaic attenuation, septal thickening or a filling mass are differential clues, not automatic WHO-group, PVOD, sarcoma, infarct or viability diagnoses. Trace actual connections and retain clinical/tissue/functional uncertainty; no treatment choice is made from the companion model.

protocol: Record source/patient, indication and actual dysphagia/acute-injury context, age/population, prior interventions and dated comparison. Identify whether this is VFSS screening, dedicated esophagram, CT/CT esophagography, MRI or separately supplied endoscopic/EUS/physiological evidence; adult guidance is not an automatic pediatric protocol.

Record actual contrast type/concentration/volume and oral or other delivery route, single/double-contrast technique, bolus/tablet if tested, projections, posture, manoeuvres, distension and obtained cervical/thoracic/EGJ/gastric extent. Record fluoroscopy pulse rate, stored frame rate/order/timestamps/gaps and spatial calibration where known.

For CT/MRI record obtained sampling, source planes/reconstructions, IV/oral contrast and phases or sequences, motion/artifact and wall/soft-tissue evaluability. For timed transit document actual ingestion/time zero, recorded acquisition times, position and calibrated retained column; no generic cutoffs are imposed on a different source protocol.

Keep endoscopic/EUS mucosal and layer evidence, pathological/assay identity, HRM/HRIM pressure or clearance, FLIP distensibility and ambulatory pH/impedance results as identified separate sources. Manometric classification requires its actual applicable protocol, anatomy and clinical context, not a fluoroscopic shape alone.

checklist.detail: Map every acquired cervical, thoracic and abdominal esophageal component and EGJ/hiatal relationship; describe actual lumen, contents and recorded transit with source coverage and uncertainty.

checklist.detail: Trace every source-resolved wall, mucosal surface and actual lesion component; retain layer, ulcer, gland/duct, neural and vascular interfaces as required anatomy while keeping unresolved microscopic tissue and identity explicit.

checklist.label: Every narrowing pouch and communication
checklist.detail: Inventory every actual ring, web, bar, stricture, pouch or communication with source site, boundary and passage effect; morphology alone does not supply cause, pressure, histology or an intervention decision.

checklist.label: Extrinsic hiatal and gastric interfaces
checklist.detail: Trace all acquired esophageal relationships to actual vessels, airways, neural routes, nodes, mediastinal tissues and hiatus/stomach; distinguish source contact or impression from supported invasion or physiological causation.

measurements.name: Stricture extent
measurements.method: Measure every actual acquired narrowing length and source-resolved minimum lumen on stated distended projection/plane with calibration, site and uncertainty.
measurements.pitfall: Distension, obliquity and projection overlap change calibre; no source measurement proves cause or safe treatment.

measurements.name: Wall lesion and extramural extent
measurements.method: Measure each acquired wall/lesion component and extension on source-supported planes; state distension, sequence/phase, edge definition and comparison.
measurements.pitfall: Collapsed lumen affects apparent thickness. Source contact is not microscopic invasion or histology.

measurements.name: Timed source retention
measurements.method: When actually obtained, record bolus/volume, posture, ingestion time zero, each real acquisition time and calibrated column height/width or observed tablet passage.
measurements.pitfall: A source protocol and timepoints must accompany observations; a static image or an unrelated threshold cannot establish motility subtype.

measurements.name: Hiatal and gastric relationships
measurements.method: Record actual EGJ/diaphragmatic relationships and herniated components or source-supported dimensions with posture, phase and coverage.
measurements.pitfall: Geometry varies during the examination; a vestibule or gastric fold landmark is not automatically a hiatal hernia, Barrett segment or physiological pressure zone.

pitfalls: A retained column or distal bird-beak pattern is a source observation; the clinical diagnosis and subtype use applicable complementary tests and context. A selected still, screening pass or static surface does not certify normal clearance, sphincter relaxation or absence of aspiration.

Plaques, ulceration, wall thickening or a reticular surface do not independently prove an organism, Barrett metaplasia, dysplasia or tumour histology. Supplied endoscopic sampling/pathology and applicable diagnostic framework stay separate; static imaging does not resolve every microscopic layer.

Smooth tapered narrowing is not proof of benignity, and shouldering is not a unique carcinoma diagnosis. Distension and projection alter apparent calibre; one unacquired or inadequately distended segment cannot be supplied as negative.

External contact, absent visible fat plane or a vascular impression alone does not establish invasion, flow direction, pressure or symptom causation. A hiatal hernia or observed reflux is not alone a diagnosis of GERD or an automatic operative indication.

No extravasation on a limited contrast study does not exclude every perforation. Pneumomediastinum, fluid or wall thickening has a differential; anatomical side or a historical pattern is not a compulsory injury site or a unique causal diagnosis.
impression_prompts: Summarise actual acquired course, wall/lumen, narrowing, lesion and adjacent/hiatal findings, source-supported transit or complications, supplied diagnosis and confidence.
State missing anatomy/time coverage and separate pathological or physiological questions. Do not automatically fill normality, histology, motility subtype, clinical stage or treatment eligibility.
escalation: Promptly communicate source findings concerning for perforation, significant leak/fistula, acute obstruction, compromised herniated tissues or another important acute complication through the appropriate clinical team, documenting uncertainty, recipient and time.

protocol: Record actual volumetric/thin-section HRCT coverage, reconstruction, inspiratory adequacy and artefacts. Expiration, prone, contrast and serial studies are separate acquired sources only when performed.

Use source-resolved lobular/tissue and airway interfaces; named CT patterns differ from clinical, pathological, genetic and physiological conclusions. Do not substitute the orientation model for actual native disease anatomy.

checklist.label: Dominant pattern
checklist.detail: Describe every actual dominant and associated ground-glass, consolidative, nodular, reticular/cystic or other pattern with source-defined site, extent, tissue interfaces and quality.

checklist.label: Distribution
checklist.detail: Record all covered side/lobe/segment and secondary-lobule/axial/pleural relationships with actual regional distribution and variant/coverage limits.

checklist.label: Fibrosis
checklist.detail: Describe each source fibrosis, distortion, traction airway, honeycomb and volume-loss component; separate the CT pattern from aetiological/multidisciplinary diagnosis.

checklist.label: Airways and air trapping
checklist.detail: Trace actual airway and regional mosaic changes; describe expiratory/prone findings only from those acquired phases with technique and source uncertainty.

checklist.label: Comparison and context
checklist.detail: Compare actual matching source sites and methods; report complications and supplied clinical/physiological context without inferring progression, pressure or function from a still.

checklist.label: Cyst morphology
checklist.detail: Trace each actual cyst or cyst-like lesion through obtained source planes; describe wall, contents, shape, septa, mural components and airway/vessel continuity with source uncertainty.

checklist.label: Distribution
checklist.detail: Record actual count/extent and regional distribution across every covered lobe, axial compartment, pleural recess and fissural/mediastinal interface; identify coverage limits.

checklist.label: Associated nodules
checklist.detail: Describe each solid/cavitating nodule, mural or intracystic component and its relationship to cysts, airways and vessels; assess actual prior change.

checklist.label: Background lung
checklist.detail: Describe intervening parenchyma, ground glass, septa, reticulation, fibrosis, honeycombing, emphysema and airway change with source phase and differential.

checklist.label: Extrapulmonary context
checklist.detail: Review pleura, pneumothorax/fluid, covered nodes and systemic findings; separate observed CT from supplied history, genetics, microbiology or tissue evidence.

checklist.label: Pattern synthesis
checklist.detail: Integrate fibrosis and cyst findings; state pattern, leading differential and interval change. UIP is not synonymous with IPF.

measurements.name: Extent and progression
measurements.method: Record source method, actual covered regions, visual/quantitative basis, phase/calibration and uncertainty for any burden estimate; compare justified matching methods/sites.
measurements.pitfall: Selected stills or a parent lung model do not supply full volumetric burden or calibrated serial change.

measurements.name: Representative cysts
measurements.method: Measure selected source-resolved lesions in stated orthogonal/local planes, wall/airspace edge convention, reconstruction/window and actual calibration; describe justified range, burden estimate and uncertainty.
measurements.pitfall: One lesion or still does not establish whole-lung burden, microscopic wall structure or calibrated serial change.

pitfalls: Ground glass alone is not fibrosis, unique inflammation, infection or a specific histology. Motion, under-inspiration, window/reconstruction and partial volume may alter apparent pattern and thin tissue borders.
A representative still cannot establish whole-lung disease absence, burden or a microscopic lobular map. State mixed patterns, each actual region and unassessed coverage.

A CT UIP pattern does not equal idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; secondary causes and multidisciplinary confidence matter. Honeycombing can overlap other fibrotic diseases; CT appearance is not the histological definition.

Do not assert no air trapping on an unperformed expiration or resolution on an unperformed prone scan. Air trapping/mosaicism alone does not uniquely diagnose HP; bronchiolocentric features can have other causes.

CT progression alone does not establish PPF. The named2022 definition uses at least two of symptoms/radiology/physiology within one year, no alternative explanation, in fibrotic ILD other than IPF. Preserve actual dates and sources; new acute opacity is not unique for exacerbation.
Dependent opacity and inadequate inspiration can mimic interstitial disease; honeycombing differs from clustered emphysematous spaces.
A thin-walled lucency is not automatically a cyst; identify airway continuity and the surrounding parenchymal pattern.

Wall thickness or apparent absence alone is not a diagnostic cutoff; partial volume, reconstruction and orientation affect thin walls. Thick/irregular components and a cyst-like cavity require a stated differential.

The source four-cysts/age-forty rule is a contextual heuristic, not a diagnosis or exclusion rule, particularly with recurrent pneumothorax or suspected hereditary disease. Costophrenic distribution supports a differential, not a unique diagnosis.

New/growing mural solid tissue or changing cyst-associated nodules warrant appropriate clinical evaluation. Wall thinning or low/negative PET uptake alone does not establish benignity; no PET finding is borrowed when PET was not obtained.

LAM/BHD-FDS/PLCH/LIP/AMP-DIP patterns overlap with infection, neoplasia, deposition and other causes. Record morphology and uncertainty; source terminology does not prove histology, genotype or functional severity.

No pneumothorax, chylous fluid, renal tumour, systemic disease or hereditary finding may be asserted from unassessed anatomy. CT fluid is not proven chyle; urgency depends on actual findings and clinical context.
impression_prompts: State source-supported dominant/mixed morphology, distribution, fibrotic features and coverage/quality limits.
Name a supported CT pattern with its reference/date and confidence; separate idiopathic/secondary or unclassifiable multidisciplinary diagnosis and missing sources.
Describe actual interval change and complications; apply named progression criteria only with the required dated radiological/clinical/physiological evidence.
escalation: Communicate actual acute respiratory/pleural/mediastinal complications through local clinical pathways; CT pattern alone does not establish physiological instability or treatment choice.

notes: Ground glass alone is not fibrosis, unique inflammation, infection or a specific histology. Motion, under-inspiration, window/reconstruction and partial volume may alter apparent pattern and thin tissue borders.
A representative still cannot establish whole-lung disease absence, burden or a microscopic lobular map. State mixed patterns, each actual region and unassessed coverage.

A CT UIP pattern does not equal idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; secondary causes and multidisciplinary confidence matter. Honeycombing can overlap other fibrotic diseases; CT appearance is not the histological definition.

Do not assert no air trapping on an unperformed expiration or resolution on an unperformed prone scan. Air trapping/mosaicism alone does not uniquely diagnose HP; bronchiolocentric features can have other causes.

CT progression alone does not establish PPF. The named2022 definition uses at least two of symptoms/radiology/physiology within one year, no alternative explanation, in fibrotic ILD other than IPF. Preserve actual dates and sources; new acute opacity is not unique for exacerbation.
Dependent opacity and inadequate inspiration can mimic interstitial disease; honeycombing differs from clustered emphysematous spaces.
A thin-walled lucency is not automatically a cyst; identify airway continuity and the surrounding parenchymal pattern.

Wall thickness or apparent absence alone is not a diagnostic cutoff; partial volume, reconstruction and orientation affect thin walls. Thick/irregular components and a cyst-like cavity require a stated differential.

The source four-cysts/age-forty rule is a contextual heuristic, not a diagnosis or exclusion rule, particularly with recurrent pneumothorax or suspected hereditary disease. Costophrenic distribution supports a differential, not a unique diagnosis.

New/growing mural solid tissue or changing cyst-associated nodules warrant appropriate clinical evaluation. Wall thinning or low/negative PET uptake alone does not establish benignity; no PET finding is borrowed when PET was not obtained.

LAM/BHD-FDS/PLCH/LIP/AMP-DIP patterns overlap with infection, neoplasia, deposition and other causes. Record morphology and uncertainty; source terminology does not prove histology, genotype or functional severity.

No pneumothorax, chylous fluid, renal tumour, systemic disease or hereditary finding may be asserted from unassessed anatomy. CT fluid is not proven chyle; urgency depends on actual findings and clinical context.
