steps.label: Dominant pattern
steps.detail: Describe every actual dominant and associated ground-glass, consolidative, nodular, reticular/cystic or other pattern with source-defined site, extent, tissue interfaces and quality.
findings: Reticular pattern with honeycombing.
Nodular pattern with [perilymphatic / centrilobular / random] distribution.
Ground-glass opacity with [crazy paving / mosaic attenuation].
Low attenuation: [centrilobular emphysema / cysts].
steps.look: Inspect thin source sections and multiple windows/reformats. Distinguish reticular septa from non-fibrotic thickening, ground glass from vessel-obscuring consolidation, cyst/mimic and every solid or airspace component. Dependent density and incomplete inspiration can simulate disease.
steps.tip: Ground glass alone is not fibrosis, unique inflammation, infection or a specific histology. Motion, under-inspiration, window/reconstruction and partial volume may alter apparent pattern and thin tissue borders.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Record all covered side/lobe/segment and secondary-lobule/axial/pleural relationships with actual regional distribution and variant/coverage limits.
findings: Basal and subpleural predominance.
Upper-zone and peribronchovascular predominance.
Subpleural sparing (NSIP pattern).
steps.look: Trace every covered lobe/actual segment and variant, central/peripheral/subpleural/peribronchovascular/perilobular compartments, fissures, pleural recesses and source-resolved secondary lobules. Identify centrilobular, perilymphatic or random nodular patterns without borrowing invisible microscopic anatomy.
steps.tip: A representative still cannot establish whole-lung disease absence, burden or a microscopic lobular map. State mixed patterns, each actual region and unassessed coverage.

steps.label: Fibrosis
steps.detail: Describe each source fibrosis, distortion, traction airway, honeycomb and volume-loss component; separate the CT pattern from aetiological/multidisciplinary diagnosis.
findings: UIP pattern: basal subpleural honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis.
Probable UIP: basal subpleural reticulation with traction bronchiectasis, no honeycombing.
Fibrosis with features of an alternative diagnosis: [ ].
steps.look: Assess actual irregular inter/intralobular septa, distortion, displacement, traction bronchi/bronchioles and honeycomb versus mimics. Review all spatial gradients and alternative/mixed features before naming UIP/probable UIP/indeterminate/alternative under a stated reference; valid unclassifiable morphology remains explicit.
steps.tip: A CT UIP pattern does not equal idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; secondary causes and multidisciplinary confidence matter. Honeycombing can overlap other fibrotic diseases; CT appearance is not the histological definition.

steps.label: Airways and air trapping
steps.detail: Trace actual airway and regional mosaic changes; describe expiratory/prone findings only from those acquired phases with technique and source uncertainty.
findings: Lobular air trapping on expiration with mosaic attenuation (hypersensitivity pneumonitis pattern with fibrosis).
Expiratory imaging not acquired.
steps.look: Trace luminal/wall changes and airway-artery relationships across actual planes. Mosaic attenuation may be airway, vascular or infiltrative; a three-density appearance on inspiration does not supply an expiratory study. Compare inspiration/expiration/prone only when actually acquired.
steps.tip: Do not assert no air trapping on an unperformed expiration or resolution on an unperformed prone scan. Air trapping/mosaicism alone does not uniquely diagnose HP; bronchiolocentric features can have other causes.

steps.label: Comparison and context
steps.detail: Compare actual matching source sites and methods; report complications and supplied clinical/physiological context without inferring progression, pressure or function from a still.
findings: Progression of fibrosis since [date].
Dilated oesophagus (systemic sclerosis context).
Pleural plaques (asbestos exposure).
steps.look: Record prior date/coverage/phase/reconstruction and comparable sites, symptoms and PFT dates/values if supplied. Review acute opacity, pleural/mediastinal air or fluid, nodes, masses and covered vascular/systemic clues with alternative causes.
steps.tip: CT progression alone does not establish PPF. The named2022 definition uses at least two of symptoms/radiology/physiology within one year, no alternative explanation, in fibrotic ILD other than IPF. Preserve actual dates and sources; new acute opacity is not unique for exacerbation.

steps.label: Cyst morphology and distribution
steps.detail: Trace each actual cyst or cyst-like lesion through obtained source planes; describe wall, contents, shape, septa, mural components and airway/vessel continuity with source uncertainty. Record actual count/extent and regional distribution across every covered lobe, axial compartment, pleural recess and fissural/mediastinal interface; identify coverage limits.
findings: Round thin-walled cysts __–__ mm, uniformly distributed (LAM pattern).
Bizarre-shaped cysts with nodules (Langerhans cell histiocytosis pattern).
Upper-zone predominance with sparing of the costophrenic angles.
Diffuse distribution including the bases.
steps.look: Use original thin sections and matching reformats, multiple windows, stated reconstruction/calibration and local axes. Distinguish cysts from cavities, bullae/emphysema, pneumatoceles, honeycombing and cystic bronchiectasis; do not infer epithelial lining or microscopic wall layers from CT. Inspect each actual covered side/lobe/region and variant: apical/basal, central/peripheral, peribronchovascular, subpleural/paramediastinal and interlobar relationships. Representative pictures cannot establish full cyst count or exclusion of disease elsewhere.
steps.tip: Wall thickness or apparent absence alone is not a diagnostic cutoff; partial volume, reconstruction and orientation affect thin walls. Thick/irregular components and a cyst-like cavity require a stated differential. The source four-cysts/age-forty rule is a contextual heuristic, not a diagnosis or exclusion rule, particularly with recurrent pneumothorax or suspected hereditary disease. Costophrenic distribution supports a differential, not a unique diagnosis.

steps.label: Cyst-associated findings and context
steps.detail: Describe each solid/cavitating nodule, mural or intracystic component and its relationship to cysts, airways and vessels; assess actual prior change. Describe intervening parenchyma, ground glass, septa, reticulation, fibrosis, honeycombing, emphysema and airway change with source phase and differential. Review pleura, pneumothorax/fluid, covered nodes and systemic findings; separate observed CT from supplied history, genetics, microbiology or tissue evidence.
findings: Centrilobular and cavitating nodules in the upper zones.
Ground glass with perivascular cysts (LIP pattern).
Ground glass with small cysts (DIP pattern).
Pneumothorax on the [ ].
Renal angiomyolipomas in the upper abdomen (tuberous sclerosis / LAM).
steps.look: Record wall nodularity/irregular thickening, intracystic material, traversing vessels and adjacent nodules/masses. Trace airway continuity and assess prior source images at matched sites without assuming registration. Assess every covered regional airway/interstitial/vascular interface. Expiratory air trapping, perfusion and dynamic behaviour require those actually acquired sources; inspiratory CT alone does not provide them. Assess actual pleura/recesses, mediastinal/hilar nodes and covered upper abdominal organs. Renal, cutaneous, genetic, infection and smoking/autoimmune context must come from supplied current source/history, not the teaching-case diagnosis.
steps.tip: New/growing mural solid tissue or changing cyst-associated nodules warrant appropriate clinical evaluation. Wall thinning or low/negative PET uptake alone does not establish benignity; no PET finding is borrowed when PET was not obtained. LAM/BHD-FDS/PLCH/LIP/AMP-DIP patterns overlap with infection, neoplasia, deposition and other causes. Record morphology and uncertainty; source terminology does not prove histology, genotype or functional severity. No pneumothorax, chylous fluid, renal tumour, systemic disease or hereditary finding may be asserted from unassessed anatomy. CT fluid is not proven chyle; urgency depends on actual findings and clinical context.

steps.label: Synthesize the pattern
steps.detail: State the imaging pattern and leading differential in clinical context.
findings: Basal subpleural fibrosis with honeycombing: UIP pattern.
Basal subpleural reticulation and traction bronchiectasis without honeycombing: probable UIP pattern, if no alternative features.
Cystic lung disease with [distribution] and [associated findings]; favour [ ].
steps.look: Combine morphology, distribution, ancillary signs and comparison.
steps.tip: UIP is an imaging pattern; IPF requires exclusion of other causes.

pitfalls: Cavitation, consolidation, nodules or an apparent fungal-ball component are not unique TB or independently proven microbiology. Missing or limited views cannot be negative disease evidence.

Imaging distribution alone does not distinguish new infection from reactivation, establish bacillary viability/infectivity, or prove drug resistance. Actual immune/clinical context must be supplied, not inferred.
Necrotic-appearing/enlarged/calcified nodes have a differential. Imaging alone does not supply tissue histology, acid-fast results, genotype or resistance status.

Imaging fluid is not proven TB/chyle or a physiological severity measurement. Possible haemoptysis-related vascular lesions or other urgent complications require actual acquired evidence and clinical assessment.

Scarring or calcification does not alone exclude coexisting active disease or establish noninfectivity. Normal imaging does not exclude latent infection or unavailable microscopic disease. State uncertainty and missing confirmation; do not infer successful treatment from unmatched stills.
impression_prompts: State actual source-supported morphology, regional extent and examination limits with a differential.
Separate imaging suspicion from supplied microbiological/clinical diagnosis, activity, infectivity and resistance status; name missing evidence.
Describe supported interval change/sequelae and urgent complications without asserting an absent history or successful treatment from unassessed sources.
escalation: Communicate source-suspected thoracic infection or urgent haemoptysis/airway/pleural/pericardial/vascular complications according to local clinical/infection-control pathways; imaging alone does not determine infectivity or management.

steps.label: Location
steps.detail: Localise the mass relative to the midline, hyoid and neck spaces, with the child's age.
findings: Midline cystic mass at the level of the hyoid.
Lateral cystic mass anterior to the sternocleidomastoid at the angle of the mandible.
Posterior triangle multiloculated mass.
steps.look: Ultrasound first: midline versus lateral; relation to the hyoid, sternocleidomastoid and thyroid.
steps.tip: Location is the strongest clue: midline suggests thyroglossal duct or dermoid cyst; anterior to sternocleidomastoid suggests a second branchial cleft cyst.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Describe cystic or solid components, septa, debris and calcification.
findings: Unilocular cyst with thin wall and internal debris.
Multiloculated cystic mass with fluid levels (lymphatic malformation).
Solid mass with calcification (pilomatrixoma / teratoma / neuroblastoma).
steps.look: Ultrasound with high-frequency probe; MRI for deep extension.

steps.label: Vascularity
steps.detail: Assess internal and peripheral flow or enhancement and vessel relationships.
findings: Avascular cyst.
Hypervascular solid mass (infantile haemangioma pattern).
Venous malformation with phleboliths and slow flow.
steps.look: Colour Doppler; contrast MRI when performed.

steps.label: Anatomic connections
steps.detail: Look for a tract, gland of origin or other structural connection, and airway effect.
findings: Cyst embedded in the strap muscles with a tract to the hyoid (thyroglossal duct cyst).
Fusiform enlargement of the sternocleidomastoid in an infant (fibromatosis colli).
Ectopic thyroid tissue with an empty thyroid bed.
steps.look: Relation to the hyoid, thyroid, salivary glands and sternocleidomastoid.
steps.tip: Confirm a normal thyroid in its bed before a midline mass is removed; it may be the only thyroid tissue.

steps.label: Nodes and infection
steps.detail: Assess nodal patterns and inflammatory complications such as abscess.
findings: Suppurative lymphadenitis with abscess __ mm.
Necrotic nodes with minimal surrounding inflammation (atypical mycobacterial pattern).
Multiple enlarged nodes without hila (lymphoma to be considered).
steps.look: Nodes: hilum, shape, necrosis; surrounding fat; collections.

checklist.label: Background
checklist.detail: Describe both actual lobes, isthmus, encountered variants/ectopic or treated tissue, acquired dimensions, parenchyma and coverage limits.

checklist.label: Nodule identification
checklist.detail: Inventory every actual relevant nodule/component; stable identity, side/site, source orthogonal dimensions and comparison. Selected index nodules do not represent all obtained anatomy.

checklist.label: Five features
checklist.detail: Use source-resolved composition, echogenicity against actual references, transverse shape, margin and echogenic foci. Name ACR framework; unavailable features remain unresolved, not zero-point findings.

checklist.label: Extension
checklist.detail: Trace each actual nodule-to-thyroid-boundary and adjacent tissue interface, with source confidence. Distinguish abutment/bulging from supported gross extension; microscopic invasion is not established by ultrasound.

checklist.label: Nodes
checklist.detail: Record actually surveyed central/lateral/other nodal regions, named map and each relevant node source morphology, dimensions and adjacent interfaces. Node evaluation is separate from nodule TI-RADS.

checklist.label: Recommendation
checklist.detail: State category and measurement separately from action. Use actual cytology/biopsy, prior treatment, clinical risk, suspicious nodes/extension and appropriate population-specific pathway.

measurements.name: Nodule size
measurements.method: For each actual relevant nodule record stable site/identity, source transverse and longitudinal planes, three orthogonal edge-to-edge dimensions, calibrated units and unresolved borders. Maximum acquired diameter is a size prompt, not all native geometry.
measurements.pitfall: Do not mix nodules, oblique planes, different acquisition/edge conventions or unresolved shadowed boundaries across comparisons.

measurements.name: Growth
measurements.method: Significant growth: at least 20% in two dimensions with at least 2 mm increase, or at least 50% volume increase.
measurements.pitfall: Compare consistent technique and account for cystic change.

classification.name: ACR TI-RADS
classification.applicability: Adult acquired thyroid-nodule ultrasound features using the named ACR framework/version. Management additionally requires applicable population, supplied biopsy and clinical risk; suspicious nodes/extension and PET-avid/pediatric contexts need the appropriate separate pathway.
classification.summary: TR1–2: no routine FNA/follow-up. TR3: FNA ≥2.5 cm, follow ≥1.5 cm. TR4: FNA ≥1.5 cm, follow ≥1 cm. TR5: FNA ≥1 cm, follow ≥0.5 cm. Confirm schedule and exceptions in the ACR reference.

pitfalls: A generic thyroid/node model or published selected frame does not represent every actual nodule, tissue boundary, node or acquired neck extent.
Do not call all comet-tail artefacts zero-point foci: use the actual ACR lexicon and source location, size and surrounding component; unresolved foci/shadowed tissue remain unresolved.
Vascularity, motion, compressibility and vessel patency require actual corresponding acquisitions; static echotexture or colour labels are not functional measurements.
Biopsy-proven status and management context are supplied clinical evidence. Growth does not make the routine unbiopsied-nodule pathway automatically applicable to a previously biopsied nodule.
impression_prompts: What is each index nodule’s point total and TR category?
Does its size and clinical context meet FNA or follow-up criteria?
Are suspicious nodes or invasive features present?
escalation: Promptly flag invasive findings or suspicious nodes for the appropriate thyroid/neck pathway.

protocol: Record side, skeletal maturity, comparison and radiographs actually obtained: AP, mortise and lateral views. Describe positioning/coverage limitations and whether images are pre- or post-reduction.

checklist.label: Fractures and mortise
checklist.detail: Inspect the medial, lateral and posterior malleoli, distal tibia and talus; describe fibular level, fracture morphology/displacement and tibiotalar alignment.

checklist.label: Syndesmosis and proximal fibula
checklist.detail: Assess tibiofibular alignment, clear spaces/overlap and syndesmotic avulsion fragments as radiographic injury clues. State proximal-fibular coverage and concern for a higher fibular injury.

checklist.label: Osseous articular surfaces
checklist.detail: Describe visible talar-dome/plafond defects, impaction, articular step/gap and posterior-malleolar extent. Separate osseous findings from direct cartilage assessment on supplemental imaging.

checklist.label: Foot and hindfoot when included
checklist.detail: For the clinically indicated region actually imaged, assess hindfoot and tarsometatarsal alignment, navicular, cuneiforms/cuboid and metatarsals. State foot or hindfoot coverage not obtained.

checklist.label: Soft tissues and modality limits
checklist.detail: Describe swelling and radiographic avulsion/alignment clues. Do not grade tendon or ligament discontinuity on radiographs; name direct integrity findings only from an appropriate acquired MRI or ultrasound examination.

measurements.name: Fracture and articular displacement
measurements.method: Measure visible fracture displacement, gap or articular step in mm with the view/plane stated. Report posterior-malleolar extent and any CT-defined impaction or articular extension separately.
measurements.pitfall: Projection limits posterior-fragment and articular measurements. A fragment percentage alone does not determine management or cartilage integrity.

measurements.name: Mortise and syndesmotic relationships
measurements.method: If measured, record medial clear space, tibiofibular clear space/overlap and talar shift with projection, positioning and weight-bearing/stress status.
measurements.pitfall: Rotation and loading alter these measurements. Normal clear spaces do not exclude ligamentous injury, and one cutoff must not be used as an automatic stability decision.

classification.name: Weber / Lauge-Hansen — with maturity and pattern limits
classification.version: Conventional fibular-level and mechanism-pattern classifications; physeal injury described separately when relevant
classification.applicability: Applicable ankle fracture patterns. These are not general foot-injury classifications and do not replace age-appropriate physeal fracture assessment.
classification.summary: Weber A/B/C describes the fibular fracture level relative to the syndesmosis. Lauge-Hansen pattern/stage requires supporting findings and stated uncertainty. Preserve the complete fracture/alignment description; do not assume stability from Weber type or intact soft tissues from radiographs.

pitfalls: A Weber B fracture is not automatically stable. A normal mortise or clear-space measurement does not exclude ligament injury.
Posterior-malleolar fractures may be subtle on a rotated lateral projection; an apparently isolated posterior or medial injury can be a clue to a wider injury pattern.
A higher fibular injury may coexist with medial or syndesmotic injury despite an unremarkable distal fibula. An ankle-only field cannot exclude injury outside its coverage.
In an immature skeleton, identify physeal, epiphyseal and metaphyseal extension and distinguish developmental centres from fragments; do not substitute an adult classification for the actual pattern.
Tendon/ligament continuity and full cartilage injury extent are not directly established on routine radiographs. Keep supplemental MRI/ultrasound findings and their modality separate.
impression_prompts: What fractures, visible articular abnormalities and alignment changes are demonstrated on the radiographs?
What syndesmotic, medial or higher-fibular injury is suspected from the observed pattern, and what remains unconfirmed?
What clinically relevant foot/hindfoot or proximal-fibular region was not imaged, and what focused question remains for supplemental assessment?
escalation: Promptly communicate fracture-dislocation, consequential malalignment or a suspected unstable injury pattern through the acute trauma pathway.
Threatened skin or neurovascular compromise requires clinical assessment; radiographs cannot establish normal skin viability, pulses or neurological function.

steps.label: Fracture map
steps.detail: Locate each malleolar fracture and relate the fibular fracture to the syndesmosis: Weber A below, B at, C above.

normal.FRACTURE MAP: No fracture of the lateral, medial or posterior malleolus.

findings: Oblique fracture of the distal fibula at the level of the syndesmosis (Weber B), running anteroinferior to posterosuperior on the lateral view, displaced __ mm.
Transverse avulsion fracture of the lateral malleolus below the syndesmosis (Weber A) [with / without] a vertical medial malleolar fracture.
Fibular fracture above the syndesmosis (Weber C), __ cm above the joint line.
Posterior malleolar fracture involving approximately __% of the tibial articular surface on the lateral view, displaced __ mm.
steps.look: Mortise and lateral views: follow the lateral malleolar cortex, then the medial malleolus, then the posterior tibial lip on the true lateral.
steps.tip: Reconstruct the mechanism: a Weber B fibular fracture with a medial malleolar fracture or a widened medial clear space is a higher-stage, potentially unstable injury.

steps.label: Mortise and talar position
steps.detail: Check that the talus is centred in the mortise and compare the medial clear space with the superior clear space.

normal.MORTISE AND TALUS: Ankle mortise congruent; medial clear space equal to the superior clear space; no talar shift or tilt.

findings: Widened medial clear space of __ mm on the [mortise / stress] view, compatible with deltoid ligament injury and lateral talar shift.
Lateral talar shift of __ mm with an incongruent mortise.
Posterior subluxation of the talus with the posterior malleolar fragment.
steps.look: True mortise view (about 15 degrees internal rotation) for clear spaces; lateral view for anterior or posterior talar subluxation.
steps.tip: The medial clear space should not exceed the superior clear space; widening without a medial malleolar fracture indicates deltoid ligament rupture.

steps.label: Syndesmosis and proximal fibula
steps.detail: Assess the distal tibiofibular relationship and decide whether the proximal fibula needs imaging.

normal.SYNDESMOSIS AND PROXIMAL FIBULA: Distal tibiofibular relationship normal; no syndesmotic avulsion.

findings: Widening of the distal tibiofibular clear space, compatible with syndesmotic injury.
Avulsion fragment at the anterior tibial tubercle (Tillaux-Chaput) or the fibular attachment of the anterior tibiofibular ligament.
Medial injury without a distal fibular fracture; the proximal fibula is not included and a Maisonneuve fracture should be excluded.
steps.look: Mortise view for tibiofibular overlap and clear space; knee or full-length fibula view when a medial injury has no matching distal fibular fracture.
steps.tip: A medial malleolar fracture or deltoid injury with an intact distal fibula should prompt a look at the proximal fibula (Maisonneuve injury).

steps.label: Articular surface
steps.detail: Describe plafond impaction, articular step or gap, posterior fragment size and talar dome injury.

normal.OSSEOUS ARTICULAR EXTENT: Tibial plafond and talar dome congruent without step, gap or impaction.

findings: Intra-articular extension with __ mm step and __ mm gap at the [plafond / medial malleolus].
Impaction of the [anterior / posterior] plafond; CT would define the fragments for surgical planning.
Osteochondral fracture of the [medial / lateral] talar dome, __ mm.
steps.look: Lateral and mortise views for step and gap; CT sagittal and axial reformats when the posterior malleolus or plafond is involved.
steps.tip: The lateral radiograph underestimates the size and comminution of a posterior malleolar fragment; CT defines it.

steps.label: Bones and osteochondral surfaces
steps.detail: Inspect the talar dome, tibial plafond and hindfoot for contusion, fracture, osteochondral lesion and accessory ossicles.

normal.BONES AND OSTEOCHONDRAL SURFACES: Normal bone marrow signal; no fracture or osteochondral lesion of the talar dome or tibial plafond.

findings: Osteochondral lesion of the [medial / lateral] talar dome, __ × __ mm and __ mm deep, [with / without] fluid signal at the fragment interface or subchondral cysts.
Bone marrow oedema of the [ ] compatible with contusion; no fracture line.
Fracture of the [lateral talar process / posterior talar process / anterior calcaneal process], seen as a T1-hypointense line.
Os trigonum with surrounding oedema and fluid, in keeping with posterior impingement in the appropriate clinical setting.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal fluid-sensitive images for marrow oedema; coronal images for the talar dome; T1 images for fracture lines.
steps.tip: Fluid signal undercutting a talar osteochondral fragment, or cysts beneath it, suggests instability.

steps.label: Lateral ligaments and syndesmosis
steps.detail: Trace the anterior and posterior tibiofibular ligaments above the joint, then the anterior talofibular, calcaneofibular and posterior talofibular ligaments.

normal.LATERAL LIGAMENTS AND SYNDESMOSIS: Anterior and posterior tibiofibular ligaments, anterior and posterior talofibular ligaments and calcaneofibular ligament intact.

findings: Complete tear of the anterior talofibular ligament at its [fibular / talar] attachment [with / without] a small avulsion fragment.
Thickened, wavy anterior talofibular ligament without discontinuity, in keeping with a chronic or healed sprain.
Tear of the anterior inferior tibiofibular ligament (syndesmotic injury) [with / without] interosseous membrane involvement.
Calcaneofibular ligament tear, indicating a more extensive lateral ligament injury.
steps.look: Axial images from the tibial plafond (tibiofibular ligaments) down to the malleolar fossa (talofibular ligaments); coronal images for the calcaneofibular ligament deep to the peroneal tendons.
steps.tip: The anterior talofibular ligament is seen at the level of the malleolar fossa; the tibiofibular ligaments lie higher, at the level of the plafond.

steps.label: Medial ligaments, sinus tarsi and plantar fascia
steps.detail: Assess the superficial and deep deltoid ligament, spring ligament, sinus tarsi and plantar fascia.

normal.MEDIAL LIGAMENTS AND SINUS TARSI: Deltoid and spring ligaments intact; sinus tarsi fat preserved; plantar fascia of normal thickness and signal.

findings: Tear of the deep deltoid (posterior tibiotalar) ligament, [partial / complete].
Spring ligament thickening or tear [with / without] posterior tibial tendon dysfunction.
Replacement of sinus tarsi fat by oedema or fibrosis, compatible with sinus tarsi syndrome in the appropriate clinical setting.
Thickened proximal plantar fascia (__ mm) with perifascial oedema, compatible with plantar fasciitis.
steps.look: Coronal and axial images for the deltoid layers; axial images beneath the talar head for the spring ligament; sagittal images for the sinus tarsi and plantar fascia.
steps.tip: The deep deltoid ligament normally looks striated because of interposed fat; this is not a tear.

steps.label: Tendons
steps.detail: Follow the medial flexors, peroneal tendons, anterior extensors and Achilles tendon from muscle to insertion.

normal.TENDONS: Flexor, extensor, peroneal and Achilles tendons of normal calibre and signal; no tenosynovitis; peroneal retinaculum intact.

findings: Posterior tibial tendinosis with [enlargement / longitudinal split / attenuation] from the medial malleolus to the navicular insertion.
Longitudinal split tear of peroneus brevis at the retromalleolar groove [with / without] peroneal tendon subluxation.
Complete Achilles tendon rupture __ cm above the calcaneal insertion with a __ mm gap.
Tenosynovitis of the [ ] tendon sheath with fluid disproportionate to the joint.
steps.look: Axial images tendon by tendon: posterior tibial, flexor digitorum longus and flexor hallucis longus medially; peroneal tendons behind the fibula; extensors anteriorly; sagittal images for the Achilles.
steps.tip: The posterior tibial tendon is normally about twice the diameter of the flexor digitorum longus; fluid in the flexor hallucis longus sheath can communicate with the ankle joint.

steps.label: Joints, impingement and soft tissues
steps.detail: Assess effusion, synovitis, capsular thickening, impingement recesses, bursae, accessory muscles and masses.

normal.JOINTS AND SOFT TISSUES: No significant ankle or subtalar effusion; no synovitis; impingement recesses clear; bursae normal.

findings: Soft-tissue thickening in the anterolateral gutter, compatible with anterolateral impingement in the appropriate clinical setting.
Retrocalcaneal bursitis with [Haglund deformity / insertional Achilles tendinopathy].
Moderate tibiotalar effusion with synovial thickening.
Accessory muscle: [peroneus quartus / accessory soleus / flexor digitorum accessorius longus].
steps.look: Sagittal images for the anterior and posterior recesses; axial images of the anterolateral gutter; sagittal images for the retrocalcaneal bursa.
steps.tip: A small amount of joint fluid is physiological; call synovitis only when the synovium is thickened.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Describe which joints are involved and spared, symmetry, and proximal or distal predominance.

normal.DISTRIBUTION: No joint-space loss, erosion or productive change in the imaged joints.

findings: Symmetric involvement of the MCP, PIP and wrist joints with relative sparing of the DIP joints (proximal, inflammatory distribution).
Predominant DIP and PIP involvement with the first carpometacarpal joint (osteoarthritis distribution).
Asymmetric involvement of DIP joints [in a ray distribution] with productive change (spondyloarthritis / psoriatic distribution).
Radiocarpal and second–third MCP predominance with chondrocalcinosis (CPPD distribution).
steps.look: Survey both hands and wrists joint by joint — DIP, PIP, MCP, carpus, radiocarpal and distal radioulnar — and any other joints included.
steps.tip: Distribution is the strongest single clue: rheumatoid arthritis is proximal and symmetric, erosive osteoarthritis central in the DIP and PIP joints, psoriatic arthritis distal and asymmetric.

steps.label: Joint spaces (cartilage)
steps.detail: Distinguish uniform from non-uniform joint-space loss and name the worst compartment.
findings: Uniform joint-space narrowing of the [ ] joints, a pattern favouring inflammatory arthritis.
Non-uniform joint-space narrowing with osteophytes and subchondral sclerosis, favouring osteoarthritis.
Ankylosis of the [carpus / interphalangeal joints].
steps.look: Well-centred PA views; compare the same joints on the prior study with the same projection and load.

steps.label: Erosions, bone formation and density
steps.detail: Characterise erosions (marginal, central, overhanging edge), osteophytes, periostitis and periarticular mineralisation.

normal.EROSIONS AND BONE RESPONSE: No erosions; no osteophytes or periostitis; normal bone mineralisation.

findings: Marginal erosions at the [ ] with periarticular osteopenia, favouring rheumatoid arthritis.
Central "gull-wing" erosions of the [DIP / PIP] joints, compatible with erosive osteoarthritis.
Erosions with fluffy periostitis and new bone formation (productive change), favouring psoriatic arthritis.
Well-defined punched-out erosions with overhanging edges and soft-tissue tophi, favouring gout.
steps.look: Bare areas at joint margins (MCP joints and ulnar styloid), central subchondral bone and shafts for periostitis; judge periarticular density.
steps.tip: Gout preserves mineralisation and joint space until late; rheumatoid arthritis causes periarticular osteopenia early.

steps.label: Alignment
steps.detail: Look for subluxation, ulnar deviation, swan-neck or boutonnière deformity, carpal collapse and ankylosis.

normal.ALIGNMENT: Normal alignment without subluxation or deformity.

findings: Ulnar deviation and volar subluxation at the MCP joints.
Carpal collapse with [scapholunate dissociation / ulnar translocation of the carpus].
Atlanto-dental interval of __ mm on flexion, compatible with atlanto-axial subluxation.
steps.look: PA and oblique hand views; lateral cervical flexion and extension views when atlanto-axial involvement is in question.
steps.tip: Deformity can be reducible; describe what the projection shows rather than inferring a fixed deformity.

steps.label: Soft tissues, calcification and change
steps.detail: Describe swelling, tophi, chondrocalcinosis or other calcification, and interval structural progression.

normal.SOFT TISSUES AND PROGRESSION: No soft-tissue swelling, calcification or tophi; no interval progression.

findings: Chondrocalcinosis of the triangular fibrocartilage, compatible with CPPD deposition.
Eccentric dense soft-tissue masses compatible with tophi.
New erosions at the [ ] since [date], indicating progression.
Fusiform periarticular soft-tissue swelling of the [ ] joints.
steps.look: Soft tissues around each joint; the triangular fibrocartilage and hyaline cartilage for chondrocalcinosis; direct comparison with the prior study.
steps.tip: Septic arthritis may be radiographically normal early; a single hot joint needs aspiration, not a pattern diagnosis.

steps.label: Location, age and margin
steps.detail: Name the bone, epiphysis, metaphysis or diaphysis, the central, eccentric, cortical or juxtacortical position, and the zone of transition, with the patient's age.

normal.LOCATION AND MORPHOLOGY: No focal bone lesion in the imaged bones.

findings: Well-defined lytic lesion with a narrow zone of transition and sclerotic margin in the eccentric metaphysis of the [bone] (non-aggressive pattern).
Ill-defined permeative or moth-eaten lesion with a wide zone of transition in the diaphysis of the [bone] (aggressive pattern).
Epiphyseal lesion in a skeletally [immature / mature] patient, __ mm.
steps.look: Radiographs in two planes first: find the lesion's centre and inspect its whole margin, then correlate with CT or MRI.
steps.tip: Age and the zone of transition are the two most informative features; a wide transition zone indicates aggressive behaviour but not a specific diagnosis.

steps.label: Matrix, periosteum and cortex
steps.detail: Describe matrix mineralisation, periosteal reaction, cortical thinning, scalloping or breach, and any pathological fracture.
findings: Chondroid matrix with rings-and-arcs calcification.
Cloud-like osteoid matrix [with / without] sunburst periosteal reaction and a Codman triangle.
Solid, uninterrupted periosteal reaction, favouring a slow-growing process.
Lamellated periosteal reaction with cortical breach.
steps.look: Radiographs and CT bone window for matrix and cortex; inspect the periosteal surface along the full length of the lesion.
steps.tip: Solid periosteal new bone suggests slow growth; interrupted, lamellated or sunburst reactions suggest an aggressive process.

steps.label: Local extent and size
steps.detail: Measure the intramedullary lesion and any extraosseous component separately in three planes.
findings: Intramedullary lesion measuring __ × __ × __ mm (series __ image __).
Extraosseous soft-tissue component measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Peritumoral oedema extending __ cm beyond the lesion margin.
steps.look: MRI T1 for marrow extent against normal fatty marrow and fluid-sensitive images for the soft-tissue component; image the whole bone when sarcoma is suspected.
steps.tip: Measure tumour extent on T1; oedema on fluid-sensitive images overstates it.

steps.label: Joint, physis and neurovascular relationships
steps.detail: State physeal or articular involvement, compartments, and the relationship to the neurovascular bundle.
findings: Tumour crosses the physis into the epiphysis; no intra-articular extension.
Soft-tissue component abuts the neurovascular bundle over less than half its circumference, without encasement.
Extension into the [ ] compartment / joint.
steps.look: Axial MRI through the soft-tissue component for the neurovascular bundle; coronal and sagittal images for the physis and joint.

steps.label: Multiplicity and comparison
steps.detail: Look for further or skip lesions and compare with prior imaging for growth.
findings: Solitary lesion; no skip lesion in the imaged bone.
Multiple lesions in [ ]; metastases, myeloma or a polyostotic benign process according to age.
Unchanged since [date], supporting a non-aggressive lesion.
steps.look: The whole imaged bone and every included bone; prior radiographs for change in size or margin.
steps.tip: In a patient over 40, consider metastasis and myeloma for any lytic lesion.

measurements.name: Lesion size
measurements.method: Measure the longest dimension and two orthogonal dimensions of the chondroid lesion on MRI or CT.
measurements.pitfall: Compare like with like; radiographic and MRI extent are not interchangeable.

measurements.name: Endosteal scalloping
measurements.method: Report the depth as a proportion of normal cortical thickness and the craniocaudal length of the scalloping.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique planes exaggerate depth; measure perpendicular to the cortex.

measurements.name: Cartilage cap
measurements.method: Measure an osteochondroma cap perpendicular to the underlying bone at its thickest point on MRI or ultrasound.
measurements.pitfall: An adjacent bursa or perichondrium can be mistaken for cap thickness.

pitfalls: Imaging features of enchondroma and atypical cartilaginous tumour overlap; describe the features that favour one rather than assigning a histological grade.
Deep endosteal scalloping (more than two-thirds of cortical thickness), cortical breach, periosteal reaction or a soft-tissue mass favour a higher-grade tumour and warrant specialist referral.

Which features favour enchondroma, atypical cartilaginous tumour or higher-grade chondrosarcoma?
Is follow-up, specialist bone-tumour review or no further imaging appropriate?
escalation: Expedite specialist review for an aggressive chondroid lesion, a lytic non-chondroid component or a pathological fracture.

steps.detail: Name the bone, central or surface location and the chondroid rings-and-arcs matrix.

steps.look: Radiographs of the whole bone and CT for rings-and-arcs calcification; decide whether the lesion is central or a surface lesion.
steps.tip: Location matters: a chondroid lesion of the pelvis, shoulder girdle or axial skeleton is more often malignant than one in the hands or feet.

steps.label: Endosteal and cortical change
steps.detail: Describe endosteal scalloping depth and length, cortical thickening, expansion, breach and periosteal reaction.

normal.ENDOSTEAL AND CORTICAL CHANGE: No endosteal scalloping, cortical change or periosteal reaction.

findings: Endosteal scalloping of about __% of cortical thickness over __ mm, without cortical breach.
Deep endosteal scalloping (more than two-thirds of the cortical thickness) with cortical thickening and expansion.
Cortical breach with periosteal reaction.
steps.look: CT or radiographs perpendicular to the cortex along the full length of the lesion.
steps.tip: Cortical thickening and expansion are signs of an active lesion even without a breach.

steps.label: MRI characteristics
steps.detail: Assess lobulated cartilage signal, entrapped fat, peritumoral oedema and enhancement pattern.
findings: Lobulated T2-hyperintense lesion with entrapped fat and peripheral septal enhancement; no peritumoral oedema.
Peritumoral marrow oedema and [early arterial / nodular] enhancement.
Loss of the lobular pattern with a T1-hypointense non-chondroid component, raising concern for dedifferentiation.
steps.look: T1 for marrow extent and entrapped fat; fat-suppressed T2 for lobulation and oedema; post-contrast (dynamic when acquired) for enhancement.
steps.tip: Preserved entrapped marrow fat favours a low-grade lesion; loss of the lobular pattern or a non-chondroid component raises concern for higher grade.

steps.label: Soft tissue and cartilage cap
steps.detail: Look for a soft-tissue mass; for an osteochondroma confirm continuity and measure the cartilage cap.
findings: Cartilage cap __ mm at its thickest point.
Cartilage cap thicker than 1.5–2 cm in a skeletally mature patient, raising concern for secondary chondrosarcoma.
Soft-tissue mass __ × __ mm extending from the lesion.
Bursa overlying the osteochondroma, __ mm.
steps.look: MRI or ultrasound perpendicular to the underlying bone at the thickest part of the cap; surrounding soft tissues.
steps.tip: Cap thickness is only reassuring after skeletal maturity; caps are normally thicker in growing children.

steps.label: Growth and grade-relevant features

steps.tip: Growth of a chondroid lesion or an osteochondroma after skeletal maturity warrants specialist review.

Calcaneal fracture with a reduced Böhler angle of __° and subtalar joint involvement.
Osteochondral lesion of the talar dome, __ mm.

Navicular [body / dorsal avulsion] fracture.

steps.label: Ulcer and sinus tract
steps.detail: Find the skin defect (marker) and trace any tract through the soft tissues to bone or joint.

normal.ULCER AND SINUS TRACT: No skin ulcer or sinus tract; subcutaneous tissues unremarkable.

findings: Ulcer beneath the [first metatarsal head / fifth metatarsal head / heel] with a sinus tract extending to the [ ].
Ulcer with surrounding cellulitis; no tract to bone.
Soft-tissue defect in direct contact with the cortex of the [ ].
steps.look: T1 and fluid-sensitive images in two planes from the skin marker to the nearest bone; post-contrast images for the tract wall.
steps.tip: Osteomyelitis in the diabetic foot almost always spreads from an adjacent ulcer; marrow change far from any ulcer suggests another cause.

steps.label: Bone marrow
steps.detail: Separate confluent medullary T1 low signal (replacement of fatty marrow) from isolated fluid-sensitive oedema.

normal.BONE MARROW: Normal marrow signal on T1 and fluid-sensitive sequences; no osteomyelitis.

findings: Confluent T1 hypointensity replacing fatty marrow in the [ ], contiguous with the ulcer tract, with corresponding fluid-sensitive signal and cortical destruction: osteomyelitis.
Fluid-sensitive marrow signal in the [ ] with preserved T1 fatty marrow: reactive osteitis rather than osteomyelitis.
Osteomyelitis extends __ mm from the [distal / proximal] end of the [ ].
steps.look: T1 images first — confluent, medullary, geographic low signal is the key sign — then fluid-sensitive and post-contrast images for extent.
steps.tip: Marrow oedema without T1 replacement of fatty marrow does not establish osteomyelitis.

steps.label: Joints and neuroarthropathy
steps.detail: Describe joint-centred distribution, subchondral oedema, fragmentation, subluxation and deformity.

normal.JOINTS AND NEUROARTHROPATHY: No neuropathic arthropathy; joint alignment normal.

findings: Acute Charcot neuroarthropathy of the [Lisfranc / Chopart] joints: periarticular subchondral marrow oedema centred on the joints, without an ulcer or tract.
Chronic Charcot foot with fragmentation, subluxation and rocker-bottom deformity.
Charcot joint with an adjacent ulcer, tract and diffuse T1 marrow replacement: superimposed osteomyelitis is likely.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial images of the Lisfranc and Chopart joints; compare the location with the ulcer.
steps.tip: Neuroarthropathy is joint-centred and midfoot-predominant; infection is ulcer-centred at pressure points. Bone margins that fade on T1 but reappear after contrast (the ghost sign) favour infection.

steps.label: Abscess and devitalised tissue
steps.detail: Look for fluid collections with rim enhancement, gas and non-enhancing (devitalised) tissue.

normal.COLLECTIONS AND VIABILITY: No abscess, gas or devitalised tissue.

findings: Rim-enhancing collection in the [medial / central / lateral plantar / dorsal] compartment measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Non-enhancing soft tissue at the [ ], compatible with devitalised tissue.
Soft-tissue gas along the [ ].
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive and post-contrast fat-suppressed images; gas appears as signal void on all sequences.
steps.tip: Without contrast, a collection and devitalised tissue cannot be separated reliably; state this limitation.

Infection spreading through the [medial / central / lateral] plantar compartment.
Amputation stump of the [ ] with [no / new] marrow signal change at the resection margin.

measurements.method: Measure partial tear extent or full-thickness retraction in mm.
measurements.pitfall: An intact lacertus fibrosus may limit retraction after distal biceps rupture.

measurements.name: Osteochondral lesion
measurements.method: Measure width, depth and detached fragment; describe fluid interface and cartilage integrity.
measurements.pitfall: Normal posterior capitellar contour can mimic a defect.

measurements.name: Nerve abnormality
measurements.method: Record segment, calibre change and any compressing lesion dimensions.
measurements.pitfall: Signal alone is nonspecific and dynamic subluxation may require ultrasound.

pitfalls: The posterior capitellar pseudodefect is a normal variant.
An accessory ossicle or synovial fold may simulate a loose body.

Is there an unstable osteochondral fragment or significant retraction?
Is neuropathy supported and is its cause visible?
escalation: Promptly flag complete acute tendon avulsion, unstable fracture/fragment or unexpected aggressive lesion when clinically consequential.

notes: Replace bracketed choices with observed findings. The gallery contains published teaching examples; cite the patient examination series and image numbers in the clinical report.

steps.label: Tendons
steps.detail: Assess the common extensor and flexor origins, the distal biceps at the radial tuberosity and the triceps at the olecranon.

normal.TENDONS: Common extensor and flexor origins, distal biceps and triceps tendons intact with normal signal.

findings: Common extensor origin tendinosis with [partial-thickness / high-grade partial / full-thickness] tear, __ mm (lateral epicondylitis).
Complete distal biceps tendon rupture retracted __ mm [with / without] an intact lacertus fibrosus.
Partial distal biceps tear with radiobicipital bursitis.
Common flexor origin tendinosis (medial epicondylitis).
steps.look: Coronal images for the common extensor and flexor origins; axial and sagittal images for the distal biceps; sagittal images for the triceps.
steps.tip: Lateral epicondylitis can coexist with a tear of the lateral ulnar collateral ligament beneath the extensor origin; look deep to the tendon.

steps.label: Collateral ligaments
steps.detail: Name the ulnar collateral ligament (anterior bundle) and lateral collateral complex components and any tear site.

normal.LIGAMENT COMPLEXES: Ulnar collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex intact.

findings: Tear of the anterior bundle of the UCL at its [humeral / sublime tubercle] attachment.
Undersurface partial tear of the distal UCL with fluid tracking along the sublime tubercle (T-sign).
Lateral ulnar collateral ligament tear, compatible with posterolateral rotatory instability in the appropriate clinical setting.
Avulsion fracture of the sublime tubercle.
steps.look: Coronal images for the anterior bundle of the UCL to the sublime tubercle and for the lateral ulnar collateral ligament behind the radial head; axial images for the annular ligament.

steps.label: Cartilage and bone
steps.detail: Inspect capitellar and trochlear cartilage, osteochondral lesions, marrow and fracture.

normal.CARTILAGE AND BONE: Articular cartilage preserved; no osteochondral lesion, marrow oedema or fracture.

findings: Osteochondral lesion of the capitellum, __ × __ × __ mm, [stable / with fluid undercutting the fragment].
Occult radial head fracture with marrow oedema.
Posteromedial olecranon osteophytes (valgus extension overload).
steps.look: Sagittal and coronal images of the capitellum and trochlea; T1 for fracture lines.
steps.tip: The pseudodefect of the capitellum lies posterolaterally at the junction with the lateral epicondyle and must not be called an osteochondral lesion.

steps.label: Nerves and muscles
steps.detail: Trace the ulnar nerve through the cubital tunnel, the radial nerve and posterior interosseous nerve at the supinator, and the median nerve; look for denervation.

normal.NERVES AND MUSCLES: Ulnar, radial and median nerves normal in calibre and signal; no denervation oedema.

findings: Ulnar nerve enlargement and increased signal in the cubital tunnel [with an anconeus epitrochlearis / osteophytes].
Denervation oedema of the supinator and extensor muscles, compatible with posterior interosseous neuropathy.
Compressing lesion [ ] along the [ ] nerve.
steps.look: Axial images from above the elbow into the proximal forearm, following each nerve.
steps.tip: Mildly increased ulnar nerve signal is common in asymptomatic elbows; enlargement and denervation are more specific.

steps.label: Joint, recesses and loose bodies
steps.detail: Review alignment, effusion, synovitis, loose bodies, synovial folds and postoperative change.

normal.JOINT AND RECESSES: Normal alignment; no effusion, synovitis or loose bodies.

findings: Joint effusion with [number] intra-articular loose bodies in the [olecranon / coronoid] fossa.
Thickened lateral synovial fold [with adjacent chondral change].
Postoperative change after [UCL reconstruction / tendon repair] with [intact / failed] repair.
steps.look: Sagittal images of the anterior and posterior recesses and olecranon fossa; coronal images for a lateral synovial fold.
steps.tip: Synovial folds and accessory ossicles can mimic loose bodies; confirm on two planes.

protocol: Record age, injured side and views. Assess AP and true lateral coverage of the elbow/distal humerus; document rotation or positioning limitations before interpreting alignment lines.

For suspected lateral condylar injury, consider an oblique view according to the local paediatric pathway. Image additional forearm/wrist sites when the clinical findings warrant it; do not infer their normality from an elbow-only field.

checklist.label: Elbow alignment
checklist.detail: Assess radiocapitellar and ulnohumeral congruity and the anterior humeral line, accounting for age, ossification and projection.

checklist.label: Ossification and growth plates
checklist.detail: Identify visible capitellar, radial-head, medial-epicondylar, trochlear, olecranon and lateral-epicondylar centres and their physes; distinguish normal developmental appearance from injury.

checklist.label: Fracture map and displacement
checklist.detail: Inspect the supracondylar region, condyles/epicondyles, proximal radius and ulna. Describe displacement, angulation, rotation and articular or physeal extension.

checklist.label: Effusion and soft tissues
checklist.detail: Assess anterior/posterior fat pads, periarticular swelling and visible soft-tissue abnormality; a fracture may remain occult.

checklist.label: Associated injury and reduction
checklist.detail: Search for dislocation or an entrapped fragment, review included forearm injury, and describe reduction/fixation when present. Radiographs do not establish normal clinical neurovascular status.

measurements.name: Fragment displacement
measurements.method: Name the fragment, projection and displacement in mm; report angular/rotational deformity separately.
measurements.pitfall: Projection and unossified cartilage can conceal the full articular extent, particularly at the lateral condyle.

measurements.name: Anterior humeral line
measurements.method: On a true lateral image, describe where the anterior humeral cortical line intersects the visible capitellar ossification centre.
measurements.pitfall: The relationship varies with age, especially in younger children. Do not diagnose a fracture solely because the line fails to cross the middle third.

measurements.name: Radiocapitellar line
measurements.method: State the view and radial landmark used; assess the radial-neck axis relative to the visible capitellum and the overall joint relationship.
measurements.pitfall: Age, forearm rotation and imperfect projection affect this line; an isolated line abnormality is not sufficient to establish dislocation.

classification.name: Gartland — when applicable
classification.version: Conventional extension-type supracondylar fracture classification; describe morphology with any assigned type
classification.applicability: Extension-type supracondylar distal humeral fracture only; not lateral condylar, epicondylar, radial-neck or olecranon injuries.
classification.summary: Use the applicable named system only after identifying the fracture pattern. Preserve the observed displacement and cortical-contact description; a classification label alone does not describe neurovascular status or determine treatment.

pitfalls: Normal ossification and unfused growth plates vary with age; an adult elbow model cannot establish paediatric normality.
An elevated anterior fat pad or visible posterior fat pad can indicate an effusion with an occult fracture; absence of a visible fracture line is not proof of no injury.
Alignment lines are age- and projection-dependent; interpret them with the other radiographic and clinical findings.
A displaced medial epicondylar fragment may become incarcerated in the joint after dislocation. Unossified cartilage may hide lateral-condylar articular extension.
impression_prompts: What fracture or dislocation is identified, with which displacement and physeal/articular involvement?
Is there an effusion or other evidence of an occult injury despite an inapparent fracture line?
What associated injury, imaging limitation or reduction/fixation finding changes the next assessment?
escalation: Promptly communicate displaced/unstable fractures, fracture-dislocation or suspected intra-articular fragment entrapment through the local paediatric pathway.
Urgent clinical assessment is required for suspected neurovascular compromise or an open injury; normal radiographic alignment does not exclude these clinical emergencies.

steps.label: Side, age and technique
steps.detail: Side [ ]; age [ ]; views [ ]; true lateral adequacy [ ]; rotation/coverage limitations [ ]; comparison [ ].
findings: Side [ ]; age [ ]; views [ ]; true lateral adequacy [ ]; rotation/coverage limitations [ ]; comparison [ ].
steps.look: Review the acquired examinations and their coverage before completing this field. For suspected lateral condylar injury, consider an oblique view according to the local paediatric pathway. Image additional forearm/wrist sites when the clinical findings warrant it; do not infer their normality from an elbow-only field.

steps.label: Alignment lines
steps.detail: Check the anterior humeral line on the true lateral and the radiocapitellar line on every view.

normal.ALIGNMENT: Anterior humeral line passes through the middle third of the capitellum; the radiocapitellar line is aligned on all views.

findings: Anterior humeral line passes anterior to the middle third of the capitellum: posterior displacement of the capitellum (extension-type supracondylar fracture).
Radiocapitellar line misses the capitellum: radial head dislocation; examine the ulna for a Monteggia fracture.
steps.look: True lateral: the anterior humeral line should cross the middle third of the capitellum. Every view: the radiocapitellar line should pass through the capitellum.
steps.tip: In very young children with a small capitellum the anterior humeral line may pass through its anterior third; use age and a true lateral before calling displacement.

steps.label: Ossification centres (CRITOE)
steps.detail: Match the visible centres to age in the order capitellum, radial head, internal (medial) epicondyle, trochlea, olecranon, external (lateral) epicondyle.

normal.OSSIFICATION AND GROWTH PLATES: Ossification centres appropriate for age and normally positioned.

findings: Medial epicondyle ossification centre displaced __ mm [distally / into the joint].
Ossicle in the trochlear position without a normally placed medial epicondyle: entrapped medial epicondyle.
Lateral condyle fragment displaced __ mm.
steps.look: AP and lateral: count the centres and confirm the medial epicondyle sits at the medial humerus, not in the joint.
steps.tip: The centres appear at roughly 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 years (earlier in girls); the trochlea does not ossify before the medial epicondyle.

steps.label: Fracture
steps.detail: Name the fracture — supracondylar, lateral condyle, medial epicondyle, radial head or neck, olecranon — and describe displacement.
findings: Extension-type supracondylar fracture, Gartland type [I / II / III], with [posterior displacement / rotation].
Lateral condyle fracture displaced __ mm.
Radial neck fracture with __° angulation.
Medial epicondyle avulsion displaced __ mm.
steps.look: Both views: supracondylar region and posterior cortex on the lateral, lateral condyle on AP and oblique, radial neck and olecranon.
steps.tip: Lateral condyle fractures can be subtle on the AP view; displacement of 2 mm or more usually changes management.

steps.label: Fat pads and effusion
steps.detail: Look for a visible posterior fat pad or an elevated anterior fat pad as signs of a joint effusion.

normal.EFFUSION AND SOFT TISSUES: Anterior fat pad normal; posterior fat pad not visible; no effusion.

findings: Elevated anterior fat pad ("sail sign") and a visible posterior fat pad: joint effusion.
Joint effusion without a visible fracture; an occult fracture is possible, most often supracondylar.
steps.look: True lateral in 90 degrees of flexion: anterior fat pad over the coronoid fossa, posterior fat pad in the olecranon fossa.
steps.tip: On a true lateral in flexion, a visible posterior fat pad is always abnormal.

steps.label: Forearm and associated injury
steps.detail: Look for a forearm fracture with radial head dislocation, a second fracture and post-reduction alignment.

normal.ASSOCIATED AND POST-REDUCTION FINDINGS: No forearm fracture or radial head dislocation.

findings: Monteggia fracture-dislocation: ulnar [fracture / plastic bowing] with anterior radial head dislocation.
Elbow dislocation [posterolateral] [with / without] medial epicondyle avulsion.
Post-reduction alignment [satisfactory / persistent displacement].
steps.look: Include the forearm when the radiocapitellar line is disrupted: look for ulnar fracture or plastic bowing.

measurements.name: Migration/subsidence
measurements.method: Use stable bony landmarks on comparable projections and report change in mm.
measurements.pitfall: A rotated projection can mimic interval component movement.

measurements.name: Lucency map
measurements.method: State zone, maximal width and progression; separate focal osteolysis from a thin stable interface.
measurements.pitfall: Radiographs cannot reliably distinguish aseptic loosening from infection.

pitfalls: Early postoperative appearance and stable expected interface change depend on implant design.
Avoid diagnosing infection solely from a lucent interface.
impression_prompts: Is the implant aligned and stable compared with prior imaging?
Is there wear, progressive loosening, fracture or dislocation?
Does the imaging pattern warrant targeted infection or soft-tissue assessment?
escalation: Promptly communicate prosthetic dislocation or an acute displaced periprosthetic fracture.

steps.label: Component position
steps.detail: Measure cup inclination and describe cup and stem position, migration and subsidence against the earliest postoperative film.

normal.COMPONENT POSITION: Components in satisfactory position, unchanged from [date]; no migration or subsidence.

findings: Acetabular cup inclination __° relative to the inter-teardrop line.
Femoral stem subsidence of __ mm since [date].
Cup migration [medial / superior] with change in inclination since [date].
steps.look: AP pelvis centred on the symphysis: cup inclination against the inter-teardrop line and leg length; lateral view for version; stem position against the greater trochanter on the first postoperative film.
steps.tip: Compare only comparable projections; pelvic tilt and rotation alter apparent cup inclination and version.

steps.label: Bone–implant interfaces
steps.detail: Map lucent lines and osteolysis by acetabular (DeLee–Charnley) and femoral (Gruen) zones and compare with prior films.
findings: Thin, non-progressive lucent line (under 2 mm) in Gruen zone __, unchanged.
Progressive lucency of __ mm in Gruen zones __, compatible with loosening.
Focal scalloped osteolysis in DeLee–Charnley zone __ measuring __ mm, compatible with particle disease.
steps.look: AP and lateral views: acetabular zones 1–3 and femoral zones 1–7 on AP and 8–14 on the lateral.
steps.tip: A lucency wider than 2 mm, progressive widening or a circumferential lucency suggests loosening; a thin stable line can be normal.

steps.label: Bearing surface and hardware
steps.detail: Look for eccentric femoral head position (liner wear), cement mantle defects and broken components.

normal.BEARING AND HARDWARE: Femoral head concentric within the cup; cement mantle intact; no hardware fracture.

findings: Eccentric superolateral position of the femoral head within the cup, compatible with polyethylene wear.
Fracture of the [stem / cement mantle / screw].
Dissociation of the acetabular liner.
steps.look: AP pelvis: femoral head centre relative to the cup centre; cement mantle; screws, wires and stem.

steps.label: Bone stock, fracture and dislocation
steps.detail: Assess periprosthetic fracture, bone stock, dislocation and heterotopic ossification.

normal.BONE AND ALIGNMENT: No periprosthetic fracture or dislocation; no heterotopic ossification.

findings: Periprosthetic femoral fracture [around / below] the stem tip with a [loose / well-fixed] stem.
Posterior dislocation of the femoral head component.
Heterotopic ossification [Brooker class __ / described].
steps.look: The full length of the stem to its tip and the whole acetabulum; the periprosthetic cortex.
steps.tip: The film must include the whole stem tip, where periprosthetic fractures commonly occur.

steps.label: Soft tissues and comparison
steps.detail: Describe soft-tissue findings, periosteal reaction and interval change, and whether the pattern warrants an infection work-up.

normal.SOFT TISSUES AND COMPARISON: Soft tissues unremarkable; no interval change since [date].

findings: Periosteal reaction and rapidly progressive lucency since [date]; infection should be considered and aspiration may be required.
Soft-tissue mass adjacent to the prosthesis; an adverse local tissue reaction should be assessed with ultrasound or MRI.
steps.look: Soft tissues about the hip and comparison with every available prior film.
steps.tip: Infection and aseptic loosening can look identical on radiographs; rapid progression and periosteal reaction raise concern for infection.

This guide does not depict the implanted cup, liner, stem, fixation hardware or Gruen zones; assess those on the examination and its AP/lateral projections.

protocol: Begin with well-positioned AP pelvis and an appropriate lateral/Dunn view; document projection and pelvic rotation. Assess morphology and coverage on the acquired radiographs.

When MRI or MR arthrography has also been acquired, assess labrum and cartilage on small-field images; state the sequences and arthrogram status. Imaging morphology alone does not establish symptomatic impingement syndrome.

checklist.label: Femoral Morphology
checklist.detail: Assess head-neck sphericity and cam morphology at the relevant clock-face location.

checklist.label: Acetabular Coverage
checklist.detail: Assess lateral coverage and version in the context of pelvic position.

checklist.label: Labrum — if MRI acquired
checklist.detail: If MRI or MR arthrography was acquired, localise tearing, detachment and paralabral cysts. Otherwise state that the labrum is not assessed.

checklist.label: Joint space and cartilage
checklist.detail: Describe radiographic joint-space loss and subchondral change; map cartilage lesions only if MRI was acquired.

checklist.label: Alternative Pain Generators
checklist.detail: Assess additional bone/joint abnormalities on the acquired radiographs. If MRI was acquired, also assess periarticular tendons, bursae, muscles and covered pelvic structures; state limitations of coverage.

measurements.name: Alpha angle
measurements.method: State plane or radial position and the point where the head contour leaves the fitted circle.
measurements.pitfall: A single plane may miss the maximal cam prominence; angle alone does not diagnose symptomatic FAI.

measurements.name: Acetabular coverage
measurements.method: Record centre-edge measurement landmarks and radiographic positioning.
measurements.pitfall: Pelvic tilt and rotation influence apparent version and coverage.

pitfalls: Cam or pincer morphology can occur without symptoms.
Clinical diagnosis requires compatible symptoms, examination signs and imaging findings; do not infer symptomatic FAI syndrome from cam/pincer morphology alone.
impression_prompts: What morphology is present and where is associated labral/chondral damage?
Is there dysplasia or an alternative cause of pain?
Which measurement technique was used?

steps.label: Femoral head–neck morphology
steps.detail: Assess head–neck sphericity and cam morphology at the anterosuperior head–neck junction.

normal.FEMORAL MORPHOLOGY: Normal femoral head–neck offset without cam morphology.

findings: Cam morphology: osseous bump at the anterosuperior head–neck junction; alpha angle __° on the [Dunn view / radial MRI at __ o'clock].
Reduced femoral head–neck offset without a discrete bump.
Herniation pit at the anterior femoral neck.
steps.look: Dunn (45 degree) or cross-table lateral view, and radial MRI reformats at the anterosuperior (about 1–2 o'clock) head–neck junction.
steps.tip: The alpha angle depends on projection and clock-face position; always state where it was measured.

steps.label: Acetabular coverage and version
steps.detail: Measure the lateral centre-edge angle and look for crossover, posterior wall and ischial spine signs, coxa profunda or protrusio.

normal.ACETABULAR COVERAGE: Normal lateral acetabular coverage; no crossover sign, dysplasia or protrusio.

findings: Pincer morphology: lateral centre-edge angle __° [with coxa profunda / protrusio].
Crossover and posterior wall signs indicating acetabular retroversion.
Undercoverage: lateral centre-edge angle __°, compatible with acetabular dysplasia.
steps.look: A well-centred AP pelvis with the coccyx over the symphysis, 1–3 cm above it.
steps.tip: Pelvic tilt and rotation create false crossover signs; check the coccyx–symphysis relationship first.

steps.label: Labrum (if MRI acquired)
steps.detail: If MRI or MR arthrography was acquired, localise tearing, detachment and paralabral cysts; otherwise state that the labrum is not assessed.

normal.LABRUM — IF MRI ACQUIRED: Acetabular labrum intact without tear, detachment or paralabral cyst.

findings: Labrum not assessed: no MRI acquired.
Anterosuperior labral tear from __ to __ o'clock [with / without] chondrolabral detachment.
Paralabral cyst __ mm adjacent to the [ ] labrum.
steps.look: Radial or oblique small-field MRI (MR arthrography when performed) around the acetabular clock face.
steps.tip: Labral tears in femoroacetabular impingement are usually anterosuperior; relate them to the site of the cam or pincer morphology.

steps.label: Joint space and cartilage
steps.detail: Describe radiographic joint-space loss and subchondral change; map cartilage lesions only if MRI was acquired.

normal.JOINT SPACE AND CARTILAGE: Joint space preserved; no subchondral sclerosis or cysts; cartilage intact where assessed.

findings: Superolateral joint-space narrowing to __ mm with subchondral cysts: secondary osteoarthritis.
Anterosuperior acetabular chondral delamination adjacent to the cam morphology (MRI).
Focal chondral defect of the [femoral head / acetabulum], __ × __ mm.
steps.look: AP pelvis for joint space; MRI proton-density or fluid-sensitive images for acetabular and femoral cartilage.
steps.tip: Established osteoarthritis changes the treatment discussion; report joint-space width even when morphology is the question.

steps.label: Alternative pain generators
steps.detail: Assess periarticular tendons, bursae, muscles and the visible pelvic structures.
findings: Prominent anterior inferior iliac spine extending to the acetabular rim (subspine impingement morphology).
Gluteus [medius / minimus] tendinopathy [with partial tear] at the greater trochanter.
Femoral head subchondral fracture or osteonecrosis.
steps.look: The whole AP pelvis — sacroiliac joints, pubic symphysis, anterior inferior iliac spine — and MRI of periarticular tendons and bursae when acquired.

protocol: Review multiplanar T1 or PD and fluid-sensitive images with known surgery and injury mechanism.
Record graft/reconstruction or meniscal surgery because postoperative criteria differ.

checklist.label: Menisci
checklist.detail: Inspect both menisci, roots and meniscocapsular attachments for tear and displaced fragments.

checklist.label: Cruciates/collaterals
checklist.detail: Assess continuity, tear location and associated avulsion.

checklist.label: Cartilage and bone
checklist.detail: Map chondral loss, osteochondral lesions, contusions and subchondral fracture.

checklist.label: Extensor mechanism
checklist.detail: Review quadriceps/patellar tendons and patellofemoral stabilisers.

checklist.label: Joint and corners
checklist.detail: Assess effusion, loose bodies, posteromedial/lateral structures and cysts.

measurements.name: Meniscal extrusion/tear
measurements.method: Measure extrusion on a standard coronal plane and describe tear location/morphology.
measurements.pitfall: Extrusion alone does not prove a root tear; inspect the attachment.

measurements.name: Cartilage/osteochondral defect
measurements.method: Measure AP/transverse extent and depth; report instability signs.
measurements.pitfall: Partial-volume signal is not a full-thickness defect.

measurements.name: Tendon or ligament gap
measurements.method: Measure retraction/gap when complete structural discontinuity is present.
measurements.pitfall: Oedema is not equivalent to fibre disruption.

pitfalls: Postoperative meniscal signal may persist without recurrent tear.
Normal variants and intermeniscal ligaments can mimic tears.
impression_prompts: What dominant internal derangement is present?
Which associated injuries or unstable/displaced fragments matter?
Is postoperative interpretation limited?
escalation: Promptly communicate an occult fracture or dislocation-pattern multiligament injury with potential neurovascular implications.

notes: Replace bracketed choices with observed findings. The gallery contains published teaching examples; cite the patient examination series and image numbers in the clinical report.

steps.label: Menisci
steps.detail: Inspect both menisci — anterior horn, body, posterior horn and roots — for tear, displaced fragment and extrusion.

normal.MENISCI: Medial and lateral menisci intact, including the roots; no extrusion or displaced fragment.

findings: [Horizontal / oblique / longitudinal / radial] tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the [inferior] articular surface.
Bucket-handle tear of the [medial] meniscus with a fragment displaced into the intercondylar notch (double PCL sign).
Posterior root tear of the [medial] meniscus with __ mm extrusion.
Fragment of the [lateral] meniscus flipped into the anterior horn region.
steps.look: Sagittal proton-density images through each meniscus from periphery to root; coronal images for the body, roots and extrusion; search the notch for displaced fragments.
steps.tip: Call a tear only when abnormal signal reaches an articular surface on at least two images, or when the meniscal shape is abnormal.

steps.label: Cruciate and collateral ligaments
steps.detail: Assess the ACL, PCL, MCL and posterolateral corner for continuity, tear site and associated avulsion.

normal.LIGAMENTS: Cruciate and collateral ligaments and posterolateral corner structures intact.

findings: Complete ACL tear with bone contusions of the lateral femoral condyle and posterolateral tibial plateau (pivot-shift pattern).
Segond fracture: avulsion from the lateral tibial rim, associated with ACL tear.
MCL injury: [periligamentous oedema / partial tear / complete tear] at the [femoral / tibial] attachment.
Posterolateral corner injury involving the [LCL / biceps femoris / popliteus tendon]; fibular head avulsion.
steps.look: Sagittal images for the cruciates; coronal images for the collateral ligaments and posterolateral corner (biceps femoris, popliteus); axial images through the posterolateral corner.
steps.tip: Posterolateral corner injuries are easily overlooked alongside an ACL tear but change surgical planning.

steps.label: Cartilage and subchondral bone
steps.detail: Map chondral loss, osteochondral lesions, contusions and subchondral fracture by compartment.

normal.CARTILAGE AND SUBCHONDRAL BONE: Articular cartilage preserved; no contusion, subchondral fracture or osteochondral lesion.

findings: Full-thickness chondral defect of the [medial femoral condyle], __ × __ mm.
Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the [medial femoral condyle] with marrow oedema.
Osteochondritis dissecans of the [lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle] with fluid undercutting the fragment (unstable).
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive images in all planes for chondral defects and contusions; T1 for fracture lines.
steps.tip: A fluid-bright line or cysts beneath an osteochondral fragment indicate instability.

steps.label: Extensor mechanism and patellofemoral joint
steps.detail: Review the quadriceps and patellar tendons, patellar position, medial patellofemoral ligament and trochlea.

normal.EXTENSOR AND PATELLOFEMORAL STRUCTURES: Quadriceps and patellar tendons intact; patella centred; medial patellofemoral ligament and retinacula intact; normal trochlea.

findings: Transient lateral patellar dislocation: medial patellofemoral ligament tear at the [femoral / patellar] attachment with medial patellar and lateral femoral condyle contusions.
Patellar tendinopathy at the inferior patellar pole.
Complete quadriceps tendon rupture with a __ mm gap.
Trochlear dysplasia with a [shallow / flat] trochlea.
steps.look: Sagittal images for the tendons; axial images for patellar position, the medial patellofemoral ligament and trochlear shape.
steps.tip: The contusion pattern of patellar dislocation (medial patella and lateral femoral condyle) persists after spontaneous reduction.

steps.label: Joint and posterior structures
steps.detail: Assess effusion, synovitis, loose bodies, popliteal cyst, posteromedial structures and postoperative change.

normal.JOINT AND POSTERIOR STRUCTURES: No significant effusion, synovitis or loose bodies; no popliteal cyst.

findings: Moderate joint effusion with [number] loose bodies.
Popliteal cyst __ × __ mm between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus [with rupture and fluid tracking distally].
Parameniscal cyst adjacent to a [horizontal] tear of the [ ] meniscus.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal images of the suprapatellar recess, Hoffa fat pad, popliteal fossa and posteromedial corner.
steps.tip: A popliteal cyst arises between the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus; a collection elsewhere needs another explanation.

protocol: Record mechanism, injury date and symptomatic site; cover the full muscle-tendon unit with T1 and fluid-sensitive sequences.
Include adjacent tendon attachment and the region of maximal oedema or haematoma; compare opposite side if useful.

checklist.label: Injured Unit
checklist.detail: Name muscle, side and compartment, including adjacent involved muscles.

checklist.label: Fibre Disruption
checklist.detail: Separate oedema without definite discontinuity from partial or complete structural disruption.

checklist.label: Tendon And Aponeurosis
checklist.detail: Assess central tendon, aponeurosis and origin/insertion.

checklist.label: Oedema And Haematoma
checklist.detail: Describe extent and compartment of oedema and blood products.

checklist.label: Associated Findings
checklist.detail: Look for neurovascular proximity, contusion, scar and alternative explanations.

measurements.name: Extent of injury
measurements.method: Report cranio-caudal oedema length, structural defect size and maximal cross-sectional involvement separately.
measurements.pitfall: Oedema dimensions are not tear dimensions.

measurements.name: Retraction
measurements.method: Measure along the tendon between the attachment or tear margins with a named plane.
measurements.pitfall: Position and muscle shortening influence the gap.

pitfalls: A generic numeric grade should not replace muscle, location and tendon involvement.
MRI morphology does not determine a precise return-to-sport date.
impression_prompts: Which unit and tissue component are disrupted?
Is there tendon involvement, complete rupture or retraction?
How extensive are oedema and haematoma?
