steps.label: Injured muscle–tendon unit
steps.detail: Name the muscle, side and compartment, and whether the injury is myofascial, myotendinous or intratendinous.

normal.INJURED UNIT: Normal muscle signal and architecture; no muscle injury.

findings: Myotendinous junction injury of the [ ] at the [proximal / mid / distal] third.
Myofascial (peripheral) injury of the [ ] with fluid along the epimysium.
Intratendinous injury of the central tendon of the [rectus femoris].
steps.look: Axial fluid-sensitive images to identify the muscle; coronal or sagittal images for the level along the unit.
steps.tip: Name the muscle and the site along the unit; myofascial, myotendinous and intratendinous injuries recover differently.

steps.label: Fibre disruption
steps.detail: Separate oedema with preserved architecture from partial or complete structural disruption.
findings: Oedema with preserved architecture (low-grade strain).
Partial fibre disruption involving approximately __% of the cross-sectional area.
Complete disruption with a __ mm gap and retraction.
steps.look: Axial and longitudinal fluid-sensitive images for loss of the normal feathery fibre pattern and discontinuity.

steps.label: Tendon and aponeurosis
steps.detail: Assess the central tendon, aponeurosis and origin or insertion.

normal.TENDON AND APONEUROSIS: Central tendon, aponeurosis and attachments intact.

findings: Central tendon disruption of the [ ] (intratendinous extension).
Avulsion of the [ ] tendon from its [origin / insertion] [with / without] a bone fragment.
steps.look: Longitudinal images along the intramuscular tendon and aponeurosis to its attachment.
steps.tip: Extension into the intramuscular tendon is associated with longer recovery than a purely myofascial injury.

steps.label: Oedema and haematoma
steps.detail: Describe the extent of oedema and the site and size of any haematoma.
findings: Oedema extends __ cm craniocaudally, involving about __% of the maximal cross-sectional area.
Intramuscular haematoma __ × __ × __ mm.
Closed degloving (Morel-Lavallée) collection between the subcutaneous fat and fascia over the [ ], __ mm.
steps.look: Fluid-sensitive images for craniocaudal oedema length; T1 and fluid-sensitive images for haematoma signal.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Look for nerve proximity, bone contusion, scar from earlier injury and alternative explanations.

normal.ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: No associated nerve, bone or fascial abnormality.

findings: Scar from previous injury at the [ ] with new adjacent oedema (re-injury).
Peripheral mineralisation within the haematoma on radiograph or CT, compatible with myositis ossificans.
Haematoma displaces the [sciatic] nerve without nerve signal change.
steps.look: Adjacent nerves, bone and fascia; comparison with earlier injuries at the same site.
steps.tip: Early myositis ossificans can mimic a soft-tissue sarcoma on MRI; radiographs or CT show its peripheral mineralisation.

protocol: Review symptom distribution, weakness, laboratory context, medication and known nerve injury; choose bilateral coverage when distribution is diagnostic.
Include T1 for fatty change and fluid-sensitive sequences for oedema; use contrast for a specific infection or mass question.

checklist.label: Distribution
checklist.detail: Map involved muscles and whether change follows a nerve, compartment or systemic pattern.

checklist.label: Oedema
checklist.detail: Describe fluid-sensitive signal and focal versus diffuse muscle involvement.

checklist.label: Fatty Change And Atrophy
checklist.detail: Use T1 to distinguish chronic fatty replacement from active oedema.

checklist.label: Collection Or Mass
checklist.detail: Identify focal lesions, blood products and enhancement if acquired.

checklist.label: Nerves And Associated Structures
checklist.detail: Inspect visible nerves, entrapment sites, tendons and bone for a cause.

measurements.name: Distribution map
measurements.method: List involved and selectively spared muscles; compare sides and proximal/distal extent.
measurements.pitfall: MRI pattern narrows the differential but does not determine a specific myopathy diagnosis.

measurements.name: Focal collection
measurements.method: Measure in three planes and describe compartment and enhancement if available.
measurements.pitfall: Oedema may occur with inflammation, infection, denervation, ischaemia or exertion.

pitfalls: Do not equate high fluid-sensitive signal with primary inflammatory myositis.
Acute denervation may produce oedema before chronic fatty atrophy appears.
impression_prompts: What distribution and combination of oedema/fatty atrophy is present?
Is a focal infection or mass identified?
Which clinical, nerve or laboratory correlation would resolve the differential?
escalation: Urgently communicate imaging concerning for aggressive soft-tissue infection or a significant abscess.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Map the involved muscles and whether the change follows a nerve, a compartment or a systemic pattern.

normal.DISTRIBUTION: Normal bulk and signal of all imaged muscles, symmetric.

findings: Symmetric proximal muscle oedema involving [ ] with relative sparing of [ ], compatible with an inflammatory myopathy in the appropriate clinical setting.
Change confined to the muscles supplied by the [ ] nerve, favouring denervation.
Selective involvement of [ ] with sparing of [ ], a pattern that may suggest [a specific myopathy].
steps.look: Bilateral axial T1 and fluid-sensitive images of the symptomatic region, muscle by muscle.
steps.tip: A distribution needs both sides; unilateral coverage can miss symmetric disease.

steps.label: Oedema
steps.detail: Describe fluid-sensitive signal, focal or diffuse involvement, and fascial and subcutaneous change.

normal.OEDEMA: No muscle, fascial or subcutaneous oedema.

findings: Diffuse muscle oedema in [ ] with perifascial fluid.
Thickening and fluid along the deep fascia [with gas]; in the appropriate clinical context this raises concern for necrotising fasciitis.
Patchy intramuscular oedema without fascial involvement.
steps.look: Fat-suppressed fluid-sensitive axial images; note fascial and subcutaneous involvement.

steps.label: Fatty change and atrophy

Unilateral fatty atrophy of the [ ] in the [ ] nerve territory (chronic denervation).

steps.tip: Acute denervation causes oedema within weeks; fatty atrophy takes months.

steps.label: Collection or mass

findings: Intramuscular abscess (pyomyositis) in the [ ] measuring __ × __ × __ mm with rim enhancement.

steps.look: Fluid-sensitive and contrast-enhanced images; diffusion if acquired.

findings: Ganglion cyst at the [ ] compressing the [ ] nerve, with denervation of [ ].
Accessory muscle: [ ].

steps.label: Cuff
steps.detail: Name involved tendon, tear surface/depth, AP extent and retraction.

normal.ROTATOR CUFF: Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis and teres minor tendons intact, with normal thickness, signal and footprint attachment.

findings: Full-thickness supraspinatus tear at the footprint, __ mm anteroposterior, retracted __ mm [lateral to / at / medial to] the humeral head apex.
Partial-thickness [articular-sided / bursal-sided / intrasubstance] [ ] tear involving approximately __% of tendon thickness, __ mm long.
Tendinosis of the [ ] tendon: thickening and intermediate signal without a fluid-signal defect.
Tear of the upper subscapularis fibres [with / without] medial displacement of the long-head biceps tendon.
steps.look: Oblique coronal fluid-sensitive images from the greater-tuberosity footprint to the musculotendinous junction; oblique sagittal images for anteroposterior tear width; axial images for the upper subscapularis fibres.
steps.tip: Magic-angle signal on short-TE images can mimic tendinopathy; confirm a defect on the long-TE fluid-sensitive sequence.

steps.label: Muscle
steps.detail: Describe atrophy and fatty infiltration for each affected cuff muscle.

normal.MUSCLE QUALITY: Normal bulk and signal of the rotator cuff muscles, without fatty infiltration or denervation oedema.

findings: Supraspinatus atrophy with a positive tangent sign.
Fatty infiltration of the [ ] muscle, [less fat than muscle / equal fat and muscle / more fat than muscle].
Oedema-like signal of the [supraspinatus / infraspinatus] muscle without a tendon tear, compatible with denervation; the [suprascapular / spinoglenoid] notch is [clear / contains a paralabral cyst].
steps.look: The most lateral oblique sagittal T1 image on which the scapular spine joins the scapular body (the Y-shaped view); compare each cuff muscle with its fossa.
steps.tip: Read the tangent sign on the most lateral Y-shaped sagittal image; more medial images make an atrophic muscle look fuller.

steps.label: Biceps
steps.detail: Review anchor, pulley, intra-articular segment and groove position.

normal.BICEPS AND PULLEY: Long-head biceps tendon intact and located in the bicipital groove; biceps anchor and pulley unremarkable.

findings: Medial [subluxation / dislocation] of the long-head biceps tendon from the bicipital groove, with an associated upper subscapularis tear.
Tendinosis of the intra-articular long-head biceps tendon with [thickening / partial-thickness tear].
Empty bicipital groove compatible with long-head biceps rupture or tenotomy; tendon stump at [level].
Tear at the biceps anchor extending from __ to __ o'clock.
steps.look: Axial images from the superior labrum down the bicipital groove; oblique sagittal images through the rotator interval for the pulley; coronal images for the biceps anchor.
steps.tip: An empty groove on axial images is a dislocation until the tendon is found medially, anterior to, within or deep to the subscapularis.

steps.label: Labrum/instability
steps.detail: Map labral injury, capsuloligamentous findings and glenoid/humeral defects.

normal.LABRUM AND INSTABILITY: Glenoid labrum intact; capsule and glenohumeral ligaments unremarkable; no Hill-Sachs or osseous Bankart lesion.

findings: Anteroinferior labral tear from __ to __ o'clock [with / without] periosteal stripping ([Bankart / Perthes / ALPSA / GLAD] pattern) and [no / an] osseous glenoid fragment.
Hill-Sachs impaction of the posterosuperior humeral head, __ mm; glenoid bone loss __% by [method].
Humeral avulsion of the inferior glenohumeral ligament (HAGL): J-shaped axillary recess.
Posterior labral tear (reverse Bankart) with reverse Hill-Sachs impaction of the anterior humeral head.
steps.look: Axial images from superior to inferior using the glenoid clock face (3 o'clock anterior); ABER images for anteroinferior labral detachment when acquired; sagittal images for the glenoid contour and the axillary recess.
steps.tip: Sublabral recess, sublabral foramen and Buford complex lie in the anterosuperior quadrant; they do not explain an anteroinferior labral defect.

steps.label: Joint/outlet
steps.detail: Assess cartilage, bursae, AC joint and associated osseous abnormality.

normal.JOINT AND OUTLET: Glenohumeral cartilage preserved; no joint effusion; subacromial-subdeltoid bursa not distended; acromion and acromioclavicular joint unremarkable.

findings: Subacromial-subdeltoid bursal fluid, [small / moderate].
Acromioclavicular joint osteoarthritis with capsular hypertrophy and inferior osteophytes [contacting / not contacting] the supraspinatus musculotendinous junction.
Os acromiale at the [pre-acromion / meso-acromion / meta-acromion] level [with / without] oedema at the synchondrosis.
Glenohumeral cartilage loss, [focal / diffuse], with [osteophytes / subchondral change].
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal images of the acromion, acromioclavicular joint and subacromial-subdeltoid bursa; superior axial images for an os acromiale; all planes for cartilage and effusion.

Do not diagnose impingement from acromial appearance alone; describe the observed dynamic finding and symptoms.

steps.label: Long head of biceps
steps.detail: Follow the tendon in the groove and rotator interval and assess stability during rotation.

normal.LONG HEAD OF BICEPS: Long-head biceps tendon in the groove with a normal fibrillar pattern; no sheath effusion; stable on dynamic rotation.

findings: Long-head biceps tendon absent from the groove, [subluxed / dislocated] medially [superficial to / within] the subscapularis.
Thickened, hypoechoic long-head biceps tendon with sheath fluid and hyperaemia (tenosynovitis).
Empty groove: long-head biceps rupture.
steps.look: Transverse and longitudinal scans in the bicipital groove with the arm externally rotated; follow into the rotator interval; dynamic internal and external rotation.
steps.tip: Anisotropy makes a tendon falsely hypoechoic; angle the probe perpendicular to the fibres before calling tendinopathy.

steps.label: Rotator cuff
steps.detail: Assess the subscapularis, supraspinatus and infraspinatus and describe any tear surface, thickness and dimensions.

normal.ROTATOR CUFF: Subscapularis, supraspinatus and infraspinatus tendons intact with normal thickness and echotexture; no calcification.

findings: Full-thickness supraspinatus tear __ × __ mm with loss of the convex bursal contour [and retraction].
Partial-thickness [articular-sided / bursal-sided] supraspinatus tear, __ mm.
Calcific deposit in the [supraspinatus], __ mm, [hard with acoustic shadowing / soft without shadowing].
Tendinosis: thickened hypoechoic supraspinatus without a defect.
steps.look: Subscapularis in external rotation; supraspinatus in the modified Crass position in long and short axis; infraspinatus posteriorly.
steps.tip: A full-thickness tear extends from the bursal to the articular surface, often with a flattened bursal contour; confirm it in two planes.

steps.label: Bursa and dynamic assessment
steps.detail: Assess subacromial–subdeltoid bursal distension and tendon and bursal movement.

normal.BURSA AND DYNAMIC ASSESSMENT: Subacromial–subdeltoid bursa not distended; smooth gliding of the cuff beneath the acromion during abduction.

findings: Subacromial–subdeltoid bursal distension of __ mm [with Doppler hyperaemia].
Bursal fluid pooling at the acromial edge with painful abduction.
steps.look: Longitudinal images over the supraspinatus at rest and during active abduction.
steps.tip: Report the observed dynamic finding and the pain it produced rather than "impingement" as a diagnosis.

steps.label: Glenohumeral recess and acromioclavicular joint
steps.detail: Review the accessible posterior joint recess and the acromioclavicular joint with focal symptom correlation.

normal.JOINT AND ACROMIOCLAVICULAR JOINT: No glenohumeral effusion in the posterior recess; acromioclavicular joint unremarkable.

findings: Glenohumeral effusion of __ mm in the posterior recess.
Acromioclavicular joint capsular distension and osteophytes [with focal tenderness].
Cortical irregularity of the greater tuberosity.
steps.look: Posterior transverse scan of the glenohumeral recess; coronal scan over the acromioclavicular joint.

steps.label: Muscles and limitations

findings: Increased echogenicity and reduced bulk of the [supraspinatus / infraspinatus] (fatty atrophy).
Cyst at the spinoglenoid notch, __ mm; MRI would assess for a labral tear.
Examination limited by [restricted movement / body habitus].

protocol: Record the CT and MRI examinations actually reviewed, coverage, reconstruction planes, image quality and comparison. Review CT bone and soft-tissue reconstructions with sagittal and coronal reformats for traumatic alignment and fracture morphology.

When MRI is acquired, review sagittal T1, T2/fluid-sensitive and targeted axial images for ligament, disc, epidural and neural injury. State when MRI was not acquired or is limited; CT alone does not directly establish ligament continuity or spinal cord signal.
Document vertebral numbering, transitional anatomy and any unexamined spinal segment. Review all included levels for additional injuries and identify an ankylosed spine or previous instrumentation.

checklist.label: Numbering and traumatic alignment
checklist.detail: Name the vertebra or motion segment and assess translation, rotation, distraction and focal angulation; document numbering and coverage limits.

checklist.label: Vertebral fracture morphology
checklist.detail: Map vertebral-body walls, one or both endplates and each posterior element. Distinguish compression/burst morphology, posterior-wall retropulsion and a transosseous distraction pattern. Note relevant bone or marrow abnormality and fracture-age evidence using the acquired modality and comparison.

checklist.label: Posterior tension band
checklist.detail: Assess spinous/interspinous and facet relationships on CT. On acquired MRI, assess supraspinous and interspinous ligaments, ligamenta flava and facet capsules separately; distinguish definite disruption from indeterminate oedema.

checklist.label: Discs and longitudinal ligaments
checklist.detail: Assess traumatic disc-space widening or disruption, endplate interfaces and anterior/posterior longitudinal ligaments with the available modality, including anterior distraction in a rigid spine.

checklist.label: Canal, epidural and neural structures
checklist.detail: Localise canal, lateral-recess or foraminal encroachment and epidural abnormality. On acquired MRI, describe cord, conus, cauda equina and named root compression or signal abnormality within coverage.

checklist.label: Paraspinal and associated injury
checklist.detail: Describe paraspinal or prevertebral soft-tissue injury, additional included fractures, postoperative limitations and other relevant visible abnormalities.

checklist.label: Classification inputs and clinical neurology
checklist.detail: Keep imaging morphology and posterior ligamentous complex assessment separate from supplied clinical neurological status. Name the applicable AO/TLICS assessment and document missing clinical information.

measurements.name: Vertebral deformity
measurements.method: At each injured level, describe vertebral height loss and local angulation with the measured surfaces, plane and comparison reference.
measurements.pitfall: Height loss or angulation alone does not determine ligament integrity, neurological status or treatment.

measurements.name: Retropulsion and canal encroachment
measurements.method: Measure posterior-wall retropulsion in mm on a stated plane/reference. If canal narrowing is quantified, identify the diameter or area method and reference level; describe the actual compartment affected.
measurements.pitfall: Do not interchange diameter and area percentages or infer clinical cord injury from osseous canal narrowing.

measurements.name: Distraction and displacement
measurements.method: Record translation, interspinous/facet separation or disc-space opening at the named motion segment, with direction, plane and relevant measurements.
measurements.pitfall: Positioning may reduce visible distraction, especially in an ankylosed spine. A vertical laminar fracture alone does not establish posterior tension-band failure.

classification.name: AO Spine thoracolumbar injury classification / TLICS
classification.version: AO Spine thoracolumbar morphology, neurology and modifiers framework (2013); TLICS (2005)
classification.applicability: Traumatic thoracic/lumbar vertebral or motion-segment injury. Classify each injured level or segment separately using the applicable framework.
classification.summary: AO morphology distinguishes compression, tension-band and translational patterns. TLICS uses morphology, posterior ligamentous complex integrity and clinical neurology. Record uncertainty and supplied clinical modifiers; do not fabricate a complete score from imaging alone or turn a label into an automatic treatment recommendation.

pitfalls: A burst fracture requires posterior vertebral-wall involvement; record which endplate or endplates are involved rather than calling every wedge deformity a burst injury.
A vertical laminar fracture accompanying compression does not by itself prove posterior tension-band failure. Assess the entire injury pattern.
MRI oedema without convincing fibre discontinuity can leave posterior ligamentous complex injury indeterminate; signal change alone must not be labelled a definite rupture.
Small anterior separation in an ankylosed spine may conceal a consequential distraction injury. Report the rigid-spine context and acquisition limitations.
Normal-appearing neural structures on imaging do not supply a clinical neurological examination. Unknown neurological status is not an intact examination.
impression_prompts: Which vertebrae or motion segments are injured, with what compression, distraction or translational morphology?
What is the evidence and certainty of posterior or anterior tension-band injury, and is further soft-tissue assessment unresolved?
What canal, epidural or neural consequence requires communication, and which clinical classification inputs or coverage remain unavailable?
escalation: Promptly communicate traumatic malalignment, suspected consequential tension-band disruption, significant canal compromise or an epidural collection with neural compression through the local trauma/spine pathway.
Report imaging/clinical neurological discordance or an incompletely assessed injury in an ankylosed spine for timely specialist correlation; do not infer clinical neurological status from the images.

steps.label: Carpal arcs (Gilula's lines)
steps.detail: Trace all three carpal arcs and check that the intercarpal joint spaces are parallel and symmetric.

findings: Scapholunate interval widened to __ mm on the PA view, compatible with scapholunate ligament injury.

steps.look: Neutral PA view: arc 1 along the proximal surfaces of the proximal row, arc 2 along its distal surfaces, arc 3 along the proximal capitate and hamate; intercarpal spaces normally about 1–2 mm.

steps.label: Lateral alignment
steps.detail: Assess the radius–lunate–capitate relationship on a true lateral view.

normal.LATERAL ALIGNMENT: Radius, lunate and capitate are collinear on the true lateral view.

findings: Perilunate dislocation: the lunate stays aligned with the radius while the capitate is dislocated dorsally.
Lunate dislocation: the lunate is tipped volarly out of the radial fossa while the capitate stays aligned with the radius.
Dorsal tilt of the lunate with a volar-flexed scaphoid (DISI pattern).
steps.look: True lateral (pisiform over the distal scaphoid pole): radius, lunate and capitate should be collinear.
steps.tip: State which bone stays aligned with the radius: the lunate in perilunate dislocation, the capitate in lunate dislocation.

steps.label: Carpal angles
steps.detail: Measure the axes with stated landmarks and describe a DISI or VISI pattern where supported.

Scapholunate angle __° (below 30°) with volar lunate tilt: VISI.
Angles not reliably measurable because of [rotation / cast].
steps.look: True lateral: scaphoid axis along its volar poles, lunate axis perpendicular to the line joining its horns, and the capitate and radius axes.
steps.tip: The normal scapholunate angle is about 30–60°; angles need a true lateral projection.

steps.label: Bones
steps.detail: Inspect for associated carpal or distal forearm fracture and chronic collapse.

findings: Scaphoid waist fracture [displaced __ mm / with humpback deformity].
Scaphoid non-union with sclerosis and cysts; proximal pole sclerosis raises concern for osteonecrosis.
Increased density and collapse of the lunate (Kienböck disease).
steps.look: Scaphoid views for waist fractures; lunate density; distal radius and ulnar styloid.

steps.label: Degenerative and dynamic findings

findings: Scapholunate advanced collapse (SLAC) pattern: radial styloid–scaphoid then capitolunate arthrosis, with the radiolunate joint preserved.
Scapholunate interval widens from __ mm to __ mm on the clenched-fist view (dynamic instability).
Scaphoid non-union advanced collapse (SNAC) pattern.

protocol: Record actual onset/last-known-well, deficit, examination times, prior treatment and comparison; identify every NCCT, CTA/MRA, perfusion, MRI or venographic component actually acquired with coverage and quality.

Review NCCT for haemorrhage and parenchymal change; review actual arch-to-vertex vascular coverage/phase and each target segment. MRI requires DWI with ADC, FLAIR and susceptibility as acquired. Venous suspicion requires appropriate actual venographic assessment rather than dense blood alone.

Check source perfusion motion, bolus, temporal sampling, truncation, coverage and processing before using estimates. Protocol/order and selection imaging follow the current clinical pathway and should avoid unnecessary reperfusion delay.

checklist.label: Haemorrhage
checklist.detail: Assess each actually acquired parenchymal, subarachnoid, ventricular and extra-axial bleeding compartment, side/site and extent; distinguish haemorrhagic transformation and unassessed limits.

checklist.label: Parenchyma
checklist.detail: Localise each acute or uncertain change by side, actual structure and vascular or venous distribution; describe applicable modality-specific MCA ASPECTS regions and separate prior injury or artefact.

checklist.label: Occlusion
checklist.detail: Assess each actually acquired arterial segment, occlusion extent, reconstitution, tandem cervical disease, stenosis/dissection and variants; assess venous findings on appropriate venography when acquired.

checklist.label: Collaterals
checklist.detail: Describe actual acquisition phases, collateral spatial extent and relative delay; retain coverage/flow/processing limitations before describing software-defined perfusion estimates.

checklist.label: Tissue and complications
checklist.detail: Assess each actual injury/estimated tissue region, oedema, shift, cisterns, ventricular obstruction, herniation, comparison and alternative diagnosis without inferring viability or current-patient findings from source examples.

measurements.name: ASPECTS
measurements.method: On an applicable MCA-territory source examination record CT or DWI modality, side, each of the ten assessed regions and acute change; score 10 minus affected regions. Retain old lesions, artefacts and unassessed regions.
measurements.pitfall: MCA ASPECTS is not a posterior circulation score, exact core volume, tissue viability assay or independent treatment rule.

measurements.name: Perfusion volumes
measurements.method: Only when acquisition/processing is adequate, record software/version, thresholds/units, estimated core and delayed region volumes in mL, mismatch volume and ratio with actual scope and uncertainty.
measurements.pitfall: Static colour maps are not numerical source maps. Motion, bolus, delay, truncation, coverage and platform effects can invalidate estimates; predicted core does not mean wholly irreversible tissue.

measurements.name: Vascular calibre and extent
measurements.method: Name the actual vessel/segment, proximal/distal lesion extent, native calibrated measurement plane, stenosis convention/reference vessel and luminal/wall findings actually resolved.
measurements.pitfall: Do not infer vessel patency from missing acquisition, a generic mesh, a dense vessel or apparent absence on a single phase. Flow, bolus and variant anatomy can mimic occlusion.

measurements.name: Midline shift and ventricular effect
measurements.method: Measure current-study shift in mm with direction, stated anatomical level and ideal-midline method; assess each acquired ventricular/cisternal compartment and obstruction/effacement.
measurements.pitfall: Selected publication slices do not establish complete extent, patient calibration, a current shift measurement or hydrocephalus.

classification.name: ASPECTS
classification.version: Ten-region MCA assessment; specify NCCT or DWI application
classification.applicability: An applicable MCA-territory examination, with actual side, regions and acquisition stated.
classification.summary: Name each affected and unassessed region with the score; keep posterior circulation and perfusion separate. Treatment selection uses the actual clinical pathway.

pitfalls: Normal early CT or an initially negative DWI does not exclude clinically consistent stroke; small/posterior lesions and acquisition limits require context.
DWI/ADC/FLAIR evolution varies. DWI–FLAIR mismatch is selection context, not an exact onset clock or an automatic treatment decision.
Predicted core and delayed tissue are imaging/processing estimates; low CBF, diffusion restriction and hypoattenuation do not prove wholly irreversible tissue.
Single-phase CTA can miss delayed filling. Collateral status does not justify avoidable delay or independently exclude reperfusion assessment.
Arterial and venous infarction can both be haemorrhagic. Dense sinus or nonterritorial injury raises a venous question; actual CTV/MRV and the clinical pathway establish the assessment.
Source cases, next-day DWI, motion/reprocessing plots and separate source patients are teaching context. They neither register to one another nor autofill the current patient report.
impression_prompts: State each actual haemorrhage or ischaemic/uncertain lesion with side/site, extent and acquisition limitations.
State each actual target arterial or venous finding, tissue/collateral estimates and urgent complication; distinguish acquired findings from unassessed questions.
Communicate the actual time-sensitive imaging question to the stroke team using current clinical/time/imaging eligibility; source scores or estimates alone do not determine treatment.
escalation: Promptly communicate acute haemorrhage, target-vessel occlusion, suspected significant venous thrombosis or threatening oedema/herniation with actual finding, limits, recipient and time.

notes: Normal early CT or an initially negative DWI does not exclude clinically consistent stroke; small/posterior lesions and acquisition limits require context.
DWI/ADC/FLAIR evolution varies. DWI–FLAIR mismatch is selection context, not an exact onset clock or an automatic treatment decision.
Predicted core and delayed tissue are imaging/processing estimates; low CBF, diffusion restriction and hypoattenuation do not prove wholly irreversible tissue.
Single-phase CTA can miss delayed filling. Collateral status does not justify avoidable delay or independently exclude reperfusion assessment.
Arterial and venous infarction can both be haemorrhagic. Dense sinus or nonterritorial injury raises a venous question; actual CTV/MRV and the clinical pathway establish the assessment.
Source cases, next-day DWI, motion/reprocessing plots and separate source patients are teaching context. They neither register to one another nor autofill the current patient report.

steps.label: Site and morphology
steps.detail: Identify the side, segment and morphology of narrowing or wall abnormality.

normal.SITE AND MORPHOLOGY: Source adequacy and coverage [__]. Each observed side, vessel segment, plaque/wall finding and unresolved source boundary [__]. Unassessed origin, branch or vessel extent [__].

findings: Calcified / soft plaque at the [right] ICA origin.
Carotid web: shelf-like intraluminal projection along the posterior wall of the ICA bulb.
Floating thrombus in the ICA.
steps.look: Trace actual covered arch origins, common carotid course, bifurcation, ICA and ECA on each side using the acquired source images and suitable reformats. Describe the supplied plaque/wall and surrounding tissue interfaces; a generic tube or selected publication view does not establish every branch or wall layer.
steps.anatomy_note: The curated right trunk reference and native CT label reference are separate source contexts, not a reconstructed bilateral current-patient carotid tree. Neither independently resolves lumen versus intima/media/adventitia or pathological plaque components.

steps.label: Residual lumen and distal calibre
steps.detail: Assess the supplied minimum lumen and distal ICA, first excluding an unsuitable or collapsed reference. Distal reduction may be threadlike or subtler and normal-appearing; retain full-collapse versus without-full-collapse distinctions.

normal.RESIDUAL LUMEN: Lumen and reference evaluability [__]. Observed minimum lumen, actual named reference site/diameter and method [__]. Distal ICA calibre, comparison ICA/ECA and possible full or subtler distal collapse [__]. Reasons grading is withheld or unresolved [__].

findings: [Side/site] source-supported conventional stenosis of [__]% by [method], with actual reference site and quality [__].

Near-occlusion concern: severe proximal narrowing with source-supported distal ICA reduction [with full collapse / without full collapse / unresolved]. No routine percentage grade is assigned to a collapsed reference.
steps.look: For suitable conventional NASCET assessment, record the actual narrowest lumen and disease-free distal ICA reference, method and plane. Review both distal ICAs, ipsilateral ECA and supplied intracranial variants/obstructions. Do not use bulb calibre, a collapsed vessel, an unvalidated model surface or an inadequate source as an interchangeable reference.
steps.tip: Near-occlusion can occur without a threadlike full collapse. Small ICA calibre alone is insufficient: assess severe proximal disease, expected calibre, comparison vessels, variants and distal disease together. Do not calculate a routine NASCET percentage from a reduced/collapsed distal reference.

steps.label: Occlusion pattern
steps.detail: Describe the stump, length of occlusion and distal reconstitution.

normal.OCCLUSION PATTERN: Actual acquisition and temporal adequacy [__]. Observed stump, non-opacified extent, distal contrast/reconstitution and uncertainty [__]. Unacquired delayed phase or distal vessel coverage [__].

findings: Occlusion of the [left] ICA from the origin with reconstitution of the [petrous / cavernous] segment.
Pseudo-occlusion: slow antegrade filling on delayed images.
steps.look: Use the actual complete covered lumen, source quality, contrast acquisition and any supplied delayed imaging to assess non-opacification, true occlusion, near-occlusion/slow filling and pseudo-occlusion from distal intracranial disease. Single-phase absence of contrast or a static MRA display cannot independently establish complete occlusion.
steps.tip: Separate source-observed non-opacification from confirmed occlusion. Record what was acquired, any unresolved timing/flow limitation and the actual distal examination; do not invent delayed-phase confirmation.

steps.label: Non-atherosclerotic causes
steps.detail: Look for dissection, fibromuscular dysplasia or other vasculopathy.

normal.OTHER CAUSES: Wall/vasculopathy source adequacy [__]. Observed flap, mural signal, channel, aneurysm or bead-like morphology [__]. Unresolved wall layers, channels and unassessed source extent [__].

findings: Dissection of the [left] ICA with crescentic mural haematoma and tapered narrowing distal to the bulb.
String-of-beads appearance (fibromuscular dysplasia).
steps.look: Inspect actual acquired wall and lumen data for dissection, flap/true-false channels, mural haematoma, pseudoaneurysm and supplied non-atherosclerotic morphology. Fat-suppressed T1 and angiographic findings require their actual acquisition context. Source diagrams illustrate concepts, not independently resolved patient wall thickness or exact dissection planes.
steps.tip: Typical location or a bead-like outline is not independent proof of tissue identity, cause or vessel patency. Describe acquired morphology and limits. Static vocal-fold medialisation in a source trauma case does not independently establish functional paralysis or a unique nerve injury.

steps.label: Intracranial run-off and comparison

normal.INTRACRANIAL AND COMPARISON: Acquired intracranial/contralateral coverage and comparison adequacy [__]. Observed runoff, collaterals, variant anatomy and source-supported interval change [__]. Unassessed vessels, perfusion and timing limitations [__].

findings: Tandem intracranial stenosis of the [ ].
Progression from __% to __% since [date].
steps.look: Trace each actually covered intracranial vessel, contralateral carotid and available collateral route. Retain anatomical variants, distal tandem obstruction, unacquired territories and comparison-method/timing limits. A visible artery or flat MRA rendering does not prove functional collateral flow, cerebral perfusion or a registered interval change.

steps.label: Global and regional atrophy
steps.detail: Describe global cortical atrophy and any regional predominance, symmetry and age appropriateness.
findings: Global cortical atrophy, GCA [2].
Asymmetric frontal and anterior temporal atrophy (frontotemporal lobar degeneration pattern).
Posterior parietal and precuneus atrophy (Koedam [2]).
steps.look: Axial FLAIR and 3D T1 in three planes; GCA scale 0–3; posterior atrophy (Koedam) on sagittal and coronal images.

steps.label: Medial temporal lobe atrophy
steps.detail: Assess both hippocampi on comparable coronal planes with the MTA score.
findings: MTA right __/4, left __/4 (abnormal for age).
Asymmetric hippocampal atrophy, [left] greater than [right].
steps.look: Coronal T1 through the hippocampal body at the level of the pons.
steps.tip: An MTA score of 2 or more under 75 years, or 3 or more at 75 and above, is usually considered abnormal.

steps.label: Vascular burden
steps.detail: Record white-matter disease (Fazekas), lacunes and strategic or territorial infarcts.

normal.SMALL-VESSEL AND ISCHAEMIC DISEASE: No significant white-matter disease (Fazekas 0–1); no infarcts.

findings: Confluent white-matter hyperintensities, Fazekas 3.
Lacunes in the basal ganglia and thalami.
Strategic infarct in the [left thalamus].
steps.look: FLAIR for white-matter lesions and lacunes; strategic sites: thalamus, caudate, angular gyrus.

steps.label: Microbleeds and siderosis
steps.detail: Describe microbleed number and distribution and cortical superficial siderosis.
findings: __ lobar microbleeds with cortical superficial siderosis (cerebral amyloid angiopathy pattern).
Deep microbleeds in the basal ganglia and pons (hypertensive pattern).
steps.look: Susceptibility-weighted or T2* images.
steps.tip: Lobar microbleeds and superficial siderosis suggest amyloid angiopathy and matter for anti-amyloid treatment eligibility.

steps.label: Treatable and alternative causes
steps.detail: Exclude mass, subdural collection, hydrocephalus, acute diffusion abnormality and other structural causes.

findings: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal widening with tight high-convexity sulci (normal pressure hydrocephalus pattern).
Cortical ribbon and deep grey diffusion restriction (Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease pattern).
Chronic subdural haematoma.
steps.look: DWI for cortical ribbon and deep grey restriction; ventricles versus sulci; subdural spaces.
steps.tip: Rapidly progressive symptoms need a different differential, including Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.

measurements.name: Collection size
measurements.method: Measure three dimensions of drainable-appearing cavity and describe location.
measurements.pitfall: Restricted diffusion and rim enhancement support but do not prove purulence.

measurements.name: Mass effect
measurements.method: Record midline shift in mm and ventricular calibre with prior comparison.
measurements.pitfall: Small strategically located lesions may cause severe obstruction.

pitfalls: Normal imaging does not exclude meningitis.
Seizure-related change, tumour and autoimmune disease can mimic infection.

Is a collection, ventriculitis or vascular complication present?

steps.label: Meningeal and cranial nerve enhancement
steps.detail: Separate pachymeningeal (dural) from leptomeningeal enhancement and note cranial nerve enhancement.

normal.MENINGES AND CRANIAL NERVES: No abnormal meningeal or cranial nerve enhancement.

findings: Smooth diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement (e.g., intracranial hypotension, post-operative).
Nodular leptomeningeal enhancement along the [cerebellar folia / basal cisterns].
Enhancement of the [ ] cranial nerve.
steps.look: Post-contrast FLAIR and T1: dural enhancement follows the inner table; leptomeningeal enhancement enters sulci and cisterns.
steps.tip: Pachymeningeal enhancement follows the skull; leptomeningeal enhancement dips into the sulci.

steps.label: Parenchymal lesions
steps.detail: Characterise the pattern — ring, nodular, gyral, perivascular — with central diffusion and surrounding FLAIR.
findings: Smooth thin ring enhancement with central restricted diffusion (abscess pattern).
Incomplete (open) ring enhancement (demyelination pattern).
Gyral enhancement of the [ ] cortex (subacute infarct / encephalitis).
Punctate and curvilinear perivascular enhancement in the pons (CLIPPERS pattern).
steps.look: Post-contrast T1 with DWI/ADC and FLAIR.
steps.tip: An open ring facing the cortex suggests demyelination; a complete smooth ring with restricted diffusion suggests abscess.

steps.label: Extra-axial collections
steps.detail: Identify subdural or epidural collections, their thickness and diffusion.
findings: Subdural empyema along the [left] convexity, __ mm thick, with restricted diffusion.
Epidural collection adjacent to the [frontal sinus].
steps.look: DWI for empyema; adjacent sinuses and bone.

steps.label: Ventricles and CSF
steps.detail: Inspect ependymal enhancement, intraventricular debris and hydrocephalus.

normal.VENTRICLES AND CSF: No ependymal enhancement, debris or hydrocephalus.

findings: Ependymal enhancement with dependent debris (ventriculitis).
Hydrocephalus with obstruction at the [ ].
steps.look: Dependent layering debris on DWI and FLAIR; ependymal surfaces.

steps.label: Vascular complications and source

findings: Venous sinus thrombosis adjacent to [mastoiditis].
Infarcts from vasculitis in the [ ].
Source: [frontal sinusitis / otomastoiditis / operative bed].
steps.look: Venous sinuses; arteries at the skull base; paranasal sinuses and mastoids.

measurements.method: Measure a suspected epileptogenic structural lesion in three planes and identify sequences.

Polymicrogyria of the [ ].

protocol: Review the actually acquired noncontrast head CT from skull base/foramen magnum through vertex in brain, wider subdural and bone windows, with multiplanar reconstructions if available.

Record acquisition coverage, reconstruction thickness/kernel, motion/beam hardening and diagnostic limitations; compare the actual prior examination and timepoint. MRI or vascular imaging, if acquired, has a separate role.

checklist.label: Extra-Axial Blood
checklist.detail: Assess each epidural, subdural and subarachnoid collection by actual side, site, extent, density pattern and relation to sutures/dural reflections.

checklist.label: Parenchymal Injury
checklist.detail: Assess every contusion, intraparenchymal haemorrhage, oedema/swelling and CT-visible traumatic axonal and/or microvascular injury; state CT sensitivity limits.

checklist.label: Ventricles
checklist.detail: Assess blood in each ventricular horn/ventricle, ventricular calibre, effacement/displacement and actual CSF-pathway obstruction or hydrocephalus.

checklist.label: Mass Effect
checklist.detail: Assess the midline at a stated level/method, basal cisterns, each suspected herniation route and secondary brainstem injury.

checklist.label: Bone And Comparison
checklist.detail: Assess skull/skull-base fractures, suture/canal involvement, pneumocephalus/scalp injury and comparable interval change.

measurements.name: Haematoma and shift
measurements.method: On the calibrated current study, measure each extra-axial collection thickness perpendicular to the adjacent skull and midline shift in mm with side/direction, a stated level (for example septum pellucidum at foramen of Monro) and a stated method.
measurements.pitfall: Perpendicular ideal-midline and A/2−B methods can differ. Uncalibrated publication PNGs or source centimetre calipers do not supply patient measurements; use comparable levels/planes for follow-up.

measurements.name: Lesion extent and interval change
measurements.method: Record each actual lesion and its extent in calibrated planes with native units, examination dates/times and comparable reconstruction; use volume only with a stated validated acquisition/method.
measurements.pitfall: Source serial panels are the source patient, not the reader patient. Density, slice plane and reconstruction differences can mimic growth; CT may miss nonhaemorrhagic injury.

measurements.name: Ventricular calibre and obstruction
measurements.method: Assess each actually imaged ventricular compartment, CSF outlet/pathway and calibre on the current study; state compression versus enlargement and the location of a suspected obstruction.

steps.label: Gland and lesion epicentre
steps.detail: Document acquisition/contrast timing, source coverage and treatment context. Localize each lesion and the actual residual gland before describing size and epicentre.

normal.GLAND AND LESION: Source adequacy [__]; gland/residual gland visualized [__]; focal observations [__]; unassessed boundaries [__].

findings: Focal [right] gland abnormality __ mm with [observed enhancement pattern]; pituitary-origin lesion considered, with source timing/limitations [__].
Sellar/suprasellar lesion __ × __ × __ mm; epicentre, residual gland and extension [__].
Midline cystic lesion with [observed signal/enhancement]; differential and unresolved components [__].
steps.look: Review available small-field coronal/sagittal T1/T2, pre/post contrast and actual dynamic frames when supplied. A single timed publication panel cannot reconstruct enhancement kinetics.
steps.tip: A selected plane does not establish the whole gland or lesion boundary. MRI morphology does not determine hormonal secretion, tissue lineage or microscopic behaviour.
steps.anatomy_note: The five-shape sella model is schematic orientation only. It does not delineate the gland capsule, optic/chiasmal fascicles, cavernous channels, ICA wall or acquired lesion surfaces. The source figures are separate publication cases, not registered to this model or the current report.

steps.label: Signal and enhancement
steps.detail: Separate acquired T1/T2/susceptibility/contrast observations from inferred tissue content; describe each solid, cystic, blood-like or unresolved component.
findings: T1-bright component [__]; blood, proteinaceous material and other causes assessed using available sequences [__].
Mixed solid/cystic lesion with [MRI observations] and [CT calcification if acquired]; differential [__].
Enhancing extra-axial/dural-based lesion with [observed features]; alternatives and unresolved interfaces [__].
steps.look: Use actual pre/post contrast and susceptibility sequences, with CT for calcification or bone when available. Record missing sequences and comparison limitations.
steps.tip: T1 brightness alone does not prove haemorrhage; enhancement or a dural tail does not establish histotype. The Part1 Figure5b caption has a published correction; retain the corrected anterior/posterior T1 description.

steps.label: Stalk and suprasellar region
steps.detail: Describe only source-resolved stalk/infundibular, posterior-lobe, hypothalamic and suprasellar relationships; retain patient age and treatment context.

normal.STALK AND SUPRASELLAR REGION: Source coverage [__]; stalk position/thickness [__]; posterior-lobe signal [__]; hypothalamic/suprasellar observations [__]; unresolved extent [__].

findings: Stalk position [__]; thickness __ mm on calibrated source images; unresolved segment [__].
Stalk thickening and posterior-lobe signal [__]; imaging differential and clinical/endocrine correlation [__].
Suprasellar/hypothalamic extension or contact [__]; acquired extent and limits [__].
steps.look: Correlate actual sagittal and coronal images. State whether posterior-lobe signal or the full stalk is assessable, and compare source ages/treatment intervals explicitly.
steps.tip: Bright-spot presence/absence and stalk morphology do not independently determine endocrine function or a specific inflammatory/neoplastic diagnosis. Follow-up source figures are not interchangeable normal anatomy.

steps.label: Optic chiasm and nerves
steps.detail: Document acquired optic nerve/chiasm/tract visibility, contact, displacement, compression and signal; identify unassessed neural segments.

normal.OPTIC PATHWAY: Optic-source adequacy [__]; visible neural structures [__]; contact/displacement/signal observations [__]; unassessed segments [__].

findings: Lesion contacts/displaces the [optic structure] at [__]; source-resolved compression and limits [__].
Optic-region signal change [__] on [sequence]; comparison and clinical visual assessment [__].
steps.look: Review actual coronal/sagittal T2 and available thin-section images. A visible contact does not by itself establish functional loss.
steps.tip: Imaging relationships and visual function remain distinct. Do not mark an unseen chiasm, optic nerve or tract as clear.

steps.label: Cavernous sinus and skull base
steps.detail: Describe imaging extension and invasion likelihood separately from microscopic invasion; inspect ICA/vascular, cavernous, dural and skull-base relationships with modality-specific limits.

normal.CAVERNOUS SINUS AND SKULL BASE: Cavernous/ICA source adequacy [__]; extension or encasement [__]; bone/sinus observations [__]; vascular differential and unresolved anatomy [__].

findings: [Right/left] cavernous extension with [observed ICA relationship]; MRI Knosp grade [__] if assessable, with invasion likelihood/limits [__].
Sellar/clival/sphenoid abnormality [__] on [MRI/CT]; actual cortical, marrow or sinus extent [__].
Possible vascular lesion based on [observed features]; unresolved thrombosis/lumen/parent-vessel relationship [__] and further assessment [__].
steps.look: Use acquired planes to document medial/central/lateral ICA tangents, extent, encasement or narrowing. Use available CT for bone and dedicated vascular imaging when vascular character remains uncertain.
steps.tip: Knosp imaging extent does not prove microscopic medial-wall invasion; the Part1 source Figure5 had no invasion found at surgery despite intermediate protrusion. A flow void alone neither confirms nor excludes an aneurysm. Resolve a suspected vascular mimic before tissue procedures.

steps.label: Dural sinuses
steps.detail: Assess each named dural sinus for patency or thrombus.
findings: Filling defect in the superior sagittal sinus (empty delta sign) extending to the [right transverse and sigmoid] sinuses.
Hyperdense [left transverse] sinus on non-contrast CT (dense clot sign).
steps.look: Non-contrast CT for dense clot or cord sign; CTV or contrast MRV source images for filling defects and the empty delta sign.
steps.tip: A hypoplastic transverse sinus or arachnoid granulation is a common mimic; check the source images.
steps.anatomy_note: The current brain atlas does not contain the dural venous sinuses.

steps.label: Deep and cortical veins
steps.detail: Inspect the deep venous system and cortical veins.
findings: Thrombosis of the internal cerebral veins and straight sinus.
Isolated cortical vein thrombosis (cord sign / susceptibility blooming).
steps.look: Internal cerebral veins, vein of Galen and straight sinus; cortical veins on susceptibility images.
steps.anatomy_note: Deep and cortical veins are not represented in this atlas. Ventricles are not venous structures.

steps.label: Parenchymal effects
steps.detail: Assess oedema, venous infarction and haemorrhage that do not follow arterial territories.

normal.PARENCHYMAL EFFECTS: No parenchymal oedema, infarction or haemorrhage.

findings: Venous oedema / infarction in the [ ] crossing arterial territories.
Bilateral thalamic oedema (deep venous thrombosis).
Haemorrhagic venous infarct __ mm.
steps.look: FLAIR and DWI; susceptibility for haemorrhage.
steps.tip: Parenchymal change that does not match an arterial territory, especially with haemorrhage, should prompt venous imaging.

steps.label: Mass effect
steps.detail: Review swelling, ventricles and herniation.
findings: Swelling with __ mm midline shift.
Effaced basal cisterns.
steps.look: Midline, ventricles and basal cisterns.

steps.label: Mimics and comparison
steps.detail: Distinguish hypoplasia, arachnoid granulations and technical signal loss, and compare patency over time.
findings: Hypoplastic [left] transverse sinus without thrombus.
Arachnoid granulation: rounded CSF-density filling defect.
Partial recanalisation since [date].
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced source images rather than time-of-flight alone.
steps.tip: Time-of-flight signal loss alone is not evidence of thrombosis.
steps.anatomy_note: Venous variants and flow-related mimics are not represented in this anatomical atlas.

steps.label: Compression
steps.detail: First exclude extrinsic cord compression and canal disease.

normal.COMPRESSION: Compression assessment [__]; actual covered levels, cause and cord/root relation [__]. Unassessed extent is not a normal finding.

findings: Cord compression at [C5–C6] by disc–osteophyte complex with cord signal change (compressive myelopathy).
Epidural mass compressing the cord at [ ].
steps.look: Sagittal T2 and axial images at every narrowed level.
steps.tip: Always exclude compression before considering an intrinsic cord disease.

steps.label: Longitudinal extent
steps.detail: Map cord signal by level and length.

normal.LONGITUDINAL EXTENT: Cord signal and longitudinal extent [__]; actual covered levels [__]; motion/partial-volume limitations [__].

findings: Short-segment lesion (under two vertebral segments) at [ ].
Longitudinally extensive lesion from [ ] to [ ] (three or more segments).
Multifocal cord lesions.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 and STIR; count vertebral segments.
steps.tip: Short peripheral lesions suggest MS; longitudinally extensive central lesions suggest NMOSD, MOGAD, ADEM or other causes.

steps.label: Axial pattern
steps.detail: Assess axial location and the proportion of the cord involved.

normal.TRANSVERSE PATTERN: Axial distribution and cross-sectional involvement [__]; each actual side/tract/horn [__]; unresolved boundaries [__].

findings: Peripheral, dorsolateral lesion involving less than half of the cross-section (MS pattern).
Central grey matter involvement (owl-eye pattern: infarction, MOGAD).
Symmetric dorsal column involvement (metabolic pattern, e.g., B12 deficiency).
steps.look: Axial T2 through each lesion.

steps.label: Calibre and enhancement
steps.detail: Assess cord expansion, atrophy and enhancement.

normal.CALIBRE AND ENHANCEMENT: Cord calibre [__]; diagnostic contrast acquired [__]; enhancement [not acquired / unassessed / pattern: __].

findings: Cord expansion with heterogeneous enhancement (tumour pattern).
Patchy enhancement of the lesion.
Cord atrophy at [ ].
steps.look: Sagittal and axial post-contrast T1.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Inspect perimedullary vessels, the conus and relevant brain findings.

normal.ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: Perimedullary vessels, conus and actually acquired brain/orbital observations [__]; unacquired regions [__].

findings: Dilated perimedullary veins on the dorsal cord with conus oedema (spinal dural arteriovenous fistula pattern).
Brain lesions typical of demyelination.
steps.look: Dorsal surface of the cord for flow voids; brain if imaged.
steps.tip: Flow voids on the dorsal cord surface with lower cord oedema suggest a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula.

steps.label: Dura and veins
steps.detail: Assess diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement and venous engorgement.

normal.DURA AND VEINS: No pachymeningeal enhancement; no venous engorgement.

findings: Smooth diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement.
Venous distension sign: convex inferior border of the dominant transverse sinus.
steps.look: Post-contrast T1; sagittal and coronal images of the transverse sinuses (convex lower border).
steps.tip: Diffuse smooth pachymeningeal enhancement with engorged sinuses is the typical cranial pattern.
steps.anatomy_note: Dura and venous structures are not represented in this atlas.

steps.label: Brain sagging
steps.detail: Review midbrain and brainstem sagging, the basal cisterns and tonsillar position.

normal.BRAIN POSITION: No brain sagging; basal cisterns normal.

findings: Sagging of the midbrain with reduced mamillopontine distance and effaced prepontine and suprasellar cisterns.
Low-lying cerebellar tonsils from brain sagging (not a congenital Chiari malformation).
steps.look: Midsagittal T1/T2: suprasellar and prepontine cisterns, mamillopontine distance, midbrain–pons angle, tonsils.
steps.tip: Tonsillar descent from sagging should not be called a Chiari I malformation.
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross cerebellar and fourth-ventricle context is highlighted. Brainstem landmarks and pathological sagging are not represented.

steps.label: Subdural collections
steps.detail: Describe subdural fluid or haematomas, their thickness and mass effect.
findings: Bilateral subdural hygromas, up to __ mm.
Subdural haematoma with mass effect.
steps.look: FLAIR and T1 over both convexities.
steps.anatomy_note: Hemisphere outlines provide orientation only; the dura and subdural collections are not represented.

steps.label: Pituitary and supportive findings
steps.detail: Assess pituitary engorgement and whether the findings fit together.

normal.OTHER SUPPORTIVE FINDINGS: Pituitary normal; no additional supportive findings.

findings: Enlarged hyperaemic pituitary gland.
Findings together give a [high / intermediate / low] Bern score probability.
steps.look: Sagittal images of the pituitary.
steps.tip: The Bern score combines these cranial signs to estimate the likelihood of a spinal CSF leak.
steps.anatomy_note: The pituitary gland and its disease-related changes are not represented in this atlas.

findings: Spinal extradural fluid from [ ] to [ ] (ventral dural tear likely).

No extradural collection; CSF-venous fistula not excluded.
steps.look: Heavily T2-weighted fat-suppressed spine MRI; dynamic myelography for localisation.
steps.tip: A normal brain MRI does not exclude a spinal CSF leak.
steps.anatomy_note: The brain atlas does not show spinal anatomy, meningeal diverticula or a spinal CSF leak.

steps.label: Gas pattern
steps.detail: Assess the stomach, proximal bowel and distal gas, including gas in the rectum.

normal.GAS PATTERN: Normal neonatal bowel gas pattern with gas in the rectum.

findings: Double bubble with no distal gas (duodenal atresia pattern).
Few dilated proximal loops (high obstruction).
Many dilated loops with no rectal gas (low obstruction).
steps.look: Supine (and horizontal-beam) abdominal radiograph: is there dilatation, how many loops, and is there gas in the rectum?
steps.tip: The number of dilated loops separates high from low obstruction; the rectal gas tells you whether obstruction is complete.

steps.label: Level of obstruction and cause
steps.detail: Describe the distribution and the likely level, and the transition when demonstrated.
findings: Duodenojejunal flexure right of the left pedicle and below the pylorus: malrotation; corkscrew duodenum suggests midgut volvulus.
Microcolon with filling defects in the terminal ileum (meconium ileus pattern).
Transition zone in the rectosigmoid with a rectosigmoid ratio below 1 (Hirschsprung pattern).
Thickened pyloric muscle __ mm, length __ mm (hypertrophic pyloric stenosis).
steps.look: Upper GI study for the duodenojejunal flexure position; contrast enema for colon calibre and transition.
steps.tip: Suspected malrotation with volvulus is an emergency; an upper GI study or ultrasound should not wait.

steps.label: Bowel wall
steps.detail: Assess mural abnormalities: pneumatosis, thickening, peristalsis and perfusion when assessed.

normal.BOWEL WALL: No pneumatosis; normal bowel wall on ultrasound where assessed.

findings: Pneumatosis intestinalis in the [right lower quadrant].
Thickened hypoperfused bowel wall on ultrasound.
steps.look: Radiograph for bubbly or linear intramural gas; ultrasound for wall thickness and Doppler.

steps.label: Free gas and fluid
steps.detail: Look for free gas, ascites and collections.
findings: Pneumoperitoneum (football sign / Rigler sign).
Complex ascites on ultrasound.
steps.look: Horizontal-beam or left lateral decubitus view; football sign and Rigler sign on supine views.

steps.label: Targeted studies and other organs
steps.detail: Record the result of any targeted study, other organ findings and limitations.
findings: Whirlpool sign of the mesenteric vessels on ultrasound (midgut volvulus).
SMV lies to the left of the SMA (malrotation).
Incarcerated inguinal hernia.
steps.look: Ultrasound of the mesenteric vessels (SMV to the right of the SMA; whirlpool sign) when malrotation is suspected.
steps.tip: The gas pattern changes with time and feeding; a normal early radiograph does not exclude an evolving emergency.

steps.tip: In children the organ of origin, together with age, narrows the differential more than the cyst appearance.

steps.label: Size and number
steps.detail: Record dimensions, multiplicity and distribution.
findings: Solitary cyst __ × __ × __ mm.
Multiple non-communicating cysts of varying size (multicystic dysplastic kidney pattern).
steps.look: Three orthogonal dimensions on ultrasound or MRI.

steps.label: Wall and contents
steps.detail: Assess simple fluid, septa, debris, fat and solid elements.
findings: Simple cyst.
Multiseptated cystic mass (lymphatic malformation pattern).
Cyst with fat and calcification (teratoma).
Echogenic layered contents (haemorrhage or debris).
steps.look: Ultrasound for echoes and septa; MRI or CT for fat and calcification.

steps.label: Flow and communication
steps.detail: Assess vascularity and any ductal, enteric or collecting-system connection.
findings: Cystic dilatation communicating with the common bile duct (choledochal cyst).
Communication with the collecting system (hydronephrosis).
Avascular septa.
steps.look: Doppler of septa and walls; continuity with the bile duct, bowel or renal pelvis.

steps.label: Mass effect and complications
steps.detail: Assess obstruction, torsion, haemorrhage and inflammation.
findings: Enlarged ovary with peripheral follicles and absent flow (torsion).
Bowel obstruction from the cyst.
Haemorrhage within the cyst.
steps.look: Adjacent bowel, ureters and vessels; ovarian flow when an adnexal cyst is present.

steps.label: Local extent

findings: Extension through the neural foramina into the spinal canal (dumbbell).

steps.label: Technique and lung volume
steps.detail: Assess rotation, inspiration and lung expansion.

normal.TECHNIQUE AND VOLUME: Supine AP radiograph without rotation; normal lung volumes.

findings: Low lung volumes.
Hyperinflated lungs.
Rotated to the [right].
steps.look: Anterior rib ends and clavicles for rotation; count ribs above the diaphragm.
steps.tip: Rotation and low volumes mimic disease in neonates.

steps.label: Lung pattern
steps.detail: Describe diffuse or focal opacity, air bronchograms and lucencies.
findings: Diffuse granular (ground-glass) opacity with air bronchograms and low volumes (respiratory distress syndrome pattern).
Streaky perihilar opacity with fluid in the fissures and normal or increased volume (transient tachypnoea pattern).
Patchy asymmetric opacity with hyperinflation (meconium aspiration pattern).
Coarse reticular opacity with cystic lucencies (bronchopulmonary dysplasia).
steps.look: Compare both lungs; look for granularity, streaky interstitial opacities or patchy asymmetric opacity.

steps.label: Air leak and pleura
steps.detail: Assess pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, interstitial emphysema and effusion.
findings: [Right] pneumothorax.
Pneumomediastinum lifting the thymus (spinnaker-sail sign).
Pulmonary interstitial emphysema of the [ ] lung.
steps.look: Anterior pneumothorax on the supine film: a hyperlucent hemithorax and sharp heart border.
steps.tip: On a supine neonatal film, a pneumothorax collects anteriorly: look for a sharp heart border and hyperlucency.

steps.label: Heart, thymus and diaphragm
steps.detail: Assess the cardiothymic silhouette and diaphragm position.
findings: Bowel loops in the left hemithorax with mediastinal shift (congenital diaphragmatic hernia).
Cardiomegaly with increased pulmonary vascularity.

steps.detail: Trace each device and locate its tip using the film anatomy.

Umbilical venous catheter tip projects over the [liver / portal vein]; not in the IVC.
Umbilical arterial catheter tip at [T8] (high position).
Gastric tube coiled in an upper oesophageal pouch (oesophageal atresia).
steps.look: Endotracheal tube between the thoracic inlet and carina; UVC tip at the IVC–right atrial junction; UAC in the high (thoracic) or low (below renal arteries) position; gastric tube in the stomach.
steps.tip: An umbilical arterial catheter goes down into the pelvis first (via the iliac artery); a venous catheter goes straight up through the liver.

steps.label: Bowel gas pattern
steps.detail: Assess distension and persistent focal loops on serial films.
findings: Diffuse bowel distension.
Persistent fixed dilated loop in the [right lower quadrant].
Gasless abdomen.
steps.look: Serial supine radiographs; a persistent loop that does not change between radiographs is an ominous sign of necrosis.

steps.label: Pneumatosis and wall
steps.detail: Look for intramural gas and wall abnormalities.
findings: Pneumatosis intestinalis in the [right lower quadrant / diffuse].
Thickened / thinned bowel wall on ultrasound.
steps.look: Bubbly or linear lucency in the bowel wall on radiographs; ultrasound for wall thickness and echogenic dots.
steps.tip: Bubbly pneumatosis can look like stool; compare with the clinical picture and serial films.

steps.label: Portal venous gas
steps.detail: Assess branching gas in the liver on radiograph or echogenic moving foci on ultrasound.
findings: Branching lucencies over the liver (portal venous gas).
Echogenic foci moving in the portal vein on ultrasound.
steps.look: Right upper quadrant on radiograph; portal vein on ultrasound.

steps.label: Free air and fluid
steps.detail: Look for pneumoperitoneum, ascites and collections.

normal.PERITONEAL FINDINGS: No free air or complex fluid.

findings: Pneumoperitoneum (football / Rigler sign): perforation.
Complex ascites with debris.
Localised collection.
steps.look: Horizontal-beam or left-side-down decubitus view; ultrasound for complex fluid.
steps.tip: Perforation is a surgical emergency; a horizontal-beam view is the most sensitive radiograph.

steps.label: Ultrasound and evolution
steps.detail: When obtained, assess perfusion and peristalsis, and describe change over time.

normal.ULTRASOUND AND EVOLUTION: Ultrasound not performed. No interval change.

findings: Absent bowel wall perfusion in the [ ] (necrosis).
Worsening since [time].
Improving pattern.
steps.look: Doppler of bowel wall; comparison with previous films.

steps.label: Compartment and thymus
steps.detail: Localise the mass and distinguish it from normal thymus.

normal.COMPARTMENT: Normal thymus for age; no mediastinal mass.

findings: Anterior mediastinal mass separate from normal thymus.
Middle mediastinal cyst adjacent to the carina.
Posterior mediastinal paravertebral mass.
steps.look: Anterior mediastinum: normal thymus is soft, conforms to adjacent structures and does not compress the airway or vessels.
steps.tip: Normal thymus never compresses the airway or vessels; a mass that does is not normal thymus.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Assess soft tissue, fluid, fat and calcification.
findings: Homogeneous soft-tissue mass __ mm (lymphoma pattern).
Fat, fluid and calcification (germ cell tumour / teratoma).
Fluid-filled cyst (bronchogenic / foregut duplication cyst).
Calcified paravertebral mass (neuroblastoma pattern).
steps.look: CT attenuation or MRI signal.

steps.label: Airway
steps.detail: Describe tracheobronchial displacement or narrowing.
findings: Tracheal narrowing to __ mm (cross-sectional area reduced by about __%).
Compression of the [left main] bronchus with distal air trapping.
steps.look: Axial and coronal CT at the narrowest airway; minimum intensity projections.
steps.tip: Significant airway compression by an anterior mass is a major anaesthetic risk; communicate it directly.

steps.label: Vessels and spinal canal

normal.VESSELS AND SPINE: No vascular compression; no intraspinal extension.

findings: Compression of the superior vena cava.
Extension through the neural foramina into the spinal canal.
steps.look: Superior vena cava and pulmonary arteries; neural foramina on MRI.

steps.label: Nodes and spread

normal.NODES AND THORACIC SPREAD: No lymphadenopathy, effusion or other lesion.

findings: Bulky mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy.
Pleural / pericardial effusion.
steps.look: Hilar and mediastinal nodes; pleural and pericardial effusions.

steps.label: Suture inventory
steps.detail: Assess the metopic, sagittal, both coronal and both lambdoid sutures individually.
findings: Fused sagittal suture; other sutures patent.
Fused [right] coronal suture.
Fused metopic suture with a ridge.
steps.look: Axial CT source images and 3D rendering; ultrasound for sutures in young infants.
steps.tip: The metopic suture normally closes in infancy; a closed metopic suture alone is not trigonocephaly.

steps.label: Extent of fusion
steps.detail: Describe the affected segment, length of fusion, ridge or sclerosis and confirm on source images.
findings: Complete fusion of the sagittal suture with ridging.
Partial fusion of the [posterior] third of the sagittal suture.
steps.look: Source images along each suture; 3D rendering can hide thin patent sutures.
steps.tip: 3D segmentation can erase a thin patent suture or create an apparent gap; confirm on source images.

steps.label: Vault shape
steps.detail: Describe the skull shape pattern, asymmetry and compensatory growth.
findings: Scaphocephaly (long narrow skull) from sagittal synostosis.
Trigonocephaly with a triangular forehead from metopic synostosis.
Anterior plagiocephaly from unilateral coronal synostosis.
Parallelogram shape without suture fusion (positional plagiocephaly).
steps.look: Vertex view of the 3D rendering; cephalic index with named landmarks if used.
steps.tip: Positional plagiocephaly gives a parallelogram shape with the ear moved forward; lambdoid synostosis gives a trapezoid with the ear moved back.

steps.label: Orbits and skull base
steps.detail: Assess orbital asymmetry, cranial fossae and skull-base findings.
findings: Harlequin-eye deformity of the [right] orbit.
Hypotelorism (metopic synostosis).
steps.look: Frontal and basal views; orbital shape (harlequin eye in coronal synostosis).

steps.label: Intracranial and associated findings
steps.detail: Describe ventricles and other visible abnormality, and whether the pattern is single-suture or multisuture.

normal.INTRACRANIAL AND ASSOCIATED FINDINGS: No intracranial abnormality within the limits of the study; single-suture pattern.

findings: Multisuture synostosis, raising concern for a syndromic form.
Copper-beaten appearance of the inner table (raised intracranial pressure to be considered).
Chiari I malformation.
steps.look: Brain window of the CT or MRI.

steps.label: Standard plane
steps.detail: Confirm a valid standard coronal plane before measuring.

normal.TECHNICAL LANDMARKS: Standard plane obtained on both sides.

findings: Standard plane not obtained on the [ ] side; measurements are not reliable.
steps.look: Straight horizontal iliac line, lower limb of the ilium, and the acetabular labrum all visible (Graf standard plane).

steps.label: Bony roof (alpha angle)
steps.detail: Assess acetabular morphology and measure the alpha angle.

normal.BONY ROOF: Right alpha angle __°, left __°; good bony roof.

findings: Alpha angle __° (50–59°): physiologically immature under 3 months (Graf IIa) or delayed ossification over 3 months (IIb).
Alpha angle __° (43–49°): critical hip (Graf IIc) or decentring (D).
Alpha angle below 43°: decentred hip (Graf III / IV).
steps.look: Alpha angle between the baseline (iliac line) and the bony roof line.
steps.tip: An alpha angle of 60° or more is normal (Graf I).

steps.label: Cartilaginous roof
steps.detail: Assess the labrum and cartilaginous coverage (beta angle if used).

normal.CARTILAGINOUS ROOF: Cartilaginous roof covers the femoral head; labrum in normal position.

findings: Beta angle __°.
Labrum everted (Graf III) / inverted (Graf IV).
steps.look: Cartilage roof line from the bony rim to the labrum.

steps.label: Femoral head position

normal.FEMORAL HEAD POSITION: Femoral heads centred with coverage of 50% or more.

findings: [Left] femoral head coverage __%, decentred.

steps.label: Alignment and development
steps.detail: Assess joint alignment and age-appropriate ossification, comparing both hips.

normal.ALIGNMENT AND DEVELOPMENT: Normal alignment and ossification; symmetric hips.

steps.look: AP pelvis and frog-leg lateral; Klein line along the superior femoral neck.

findings: Flattening, sclerosis and fragmentation of the [right] femoral epiphysis (Perthes disease).
Widened irregular physis with posteromedial slip of the epiphysis.
steps.look: Epiphyseal height and density; physis width compared with the other side.

steps.label: Effusion
steps.detail: Describe effusion and synovial findings, comparing both sides.
findings: [Right] hip effusion (capsule-to-neck distance __ mm; __ mm more than the other side).
Synovial thickening with hyperaemia.
steps.look: Anterior sagittal ultrasound along the femoral neck; compare capsule distance with the other hip.
steps.tip: An effusion alone cannot separate transient synovitis from septic arthritis; aspiration is guided by the clinical picture.

steps.label: Bone and marrow
steps.detail: Review osseous change and MRI marrow findings if obtained.
findings: Metaphyseal marrow oedema with periosteal reaction (osteomyelitis).
Reduced epiphyseal enhancement (ischaemia).
Avulsion of the [anterior inferior iliac spine / ischial apophysis].
steps.look: Radiographs for lucency and periosteal reaction; MRI for marrow oedema and epiphyseal perfusion.
